dn16:0.2: The Discourse about the Great Emancipation
dn16:1.1.2: At one time the Fortunate One was living near Rājagaha on the Vultures’ Peak Mountain.
dn16:1.1.3: Now at that time the Magadhan King Ajātasattu, the son of Lady Wisdom, had a desire to attack the Vajjians.
dn16:1.1.5: “I will annihilate these Vajjians, who are so successful, so powerful, I will destroy the Vajjians, I will bring about the downfall and destruction of the Vajjians”.
dn16:1.2.1: Then the Magadhan King Ajātasattu, the son of Lady Wisdom, addressed the Magadhan chief minister the brahmin Vassakāra, (saying):
dn16:1.2.2: “Go, brahmin, and approach the Fortunate One, and after approaching worship the Fortunate One’s feet in my name, and ask whether he is free from sickness, free from illness, in good health, and living comfortably, (and say):
dn16:1.2.3: ‘The Magadhan King Ajātasattu, the son of Lady Wisdom, reverend Sir, worships with his head at the Fortunate One’s feet, and asks whether you are free from sickness, free from illness, in good health, and living comfortably.’
dn16:1.2.5: ‘The Magadhan King Ajātasattu, the son of Lady Wisdom, reverend Sir, desires to attack the Vajjians.
dn16:1.2.7: “I will annihilate these Vajjians, who are so successful, so powerful, I will destroy the Vajjians, I will bring about the downfall and destruction of the Vajjians.”
dn16:1.2.8: And just what the Fortunate One says to you, after learning it well, you must inform me,
dn16:1.2.9: for the Realised Ones do not speak falsely.”
dn16:1.3.0: “Very well, dear Sir,” and the Magadhan chief minister the brahmin Vassakāra,
dn16:1.3.1: after replying to the Magadhan King Ajātasattu, the son of Lady Wisdom, and having (many) great and august vehicles prepared, and mounting a great and august vehicle, departed with those great and august vehicles from Rājagaha, and after approaching by vehicle to the Vultures’ Peak Mountain as far as the ground for a vehicle (would allow),
dn16:1.3.2: and descending from the vehicle, he approached the Fortunate One by foot, and after approaching, he exchanged greetings with the Fortunate One,
dn16:1.3.3: and after exchanging courteous talk and greetings, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side, the Magadhan chief minister the brahmin Vassakāra said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:1.3.4: “The Magadhan King Ajātasattu, the son of Lady Wisdom, dear Gotama, worships with his head at dear Gotama’s feet, and asks whether you are free from sickness, free from illness, in good health, and living comfortably.
dn16:1.3.5: The Magadhan King Ajātasattu, the son of Lady Wisdom, dear Gotama, desires to attack the Vajjians.
dn16:1.3.7: ‘I will annihilate these Vajjians, who are so successful, so powerful, I will destroy the Vajjians, I will bring about the downfall and destruction of the Vajjians’”.
dn16:1.4.1: Now at that time venerable Ānanda was stood behind the Fortunate One fanning the Fortunate One.
dn16:1.4.2: Then the Fortunate One addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:1.4.3: “Have you heard, Ānanda: ‘The Vajjians assemble regularly and assemble frequently?’”
dn16:1.4.4: “I have heard this, reverend Sir: ‘The Vajjians assemble regularly and assemble frequently.’”
dn16:1.4.5: “For as long, Ānanda, as the Vajjians will assemble regularly and assemble frequently surely growth, Ānanda, is to be expected for the Vajjians not decline.
dn16:1.4.6: Have you heard, Ānanda: ‘The Vajjians assemble unanimously, rise unanimously, and carry out their Vajjian duties unanimously?’”
dn16:1.4.7: “I have heard this, reverend Sir, that the Vajjians assemble unanimously, rise unanimously, and carry out their Vajjian duties unanimously.”
dn16:1.4.8: “For as long, Ānanda, as the Vajjians will assemble unanimously, rise unanimously, and carry out their Vajjian duties unanimously, surely growth, Ānanda, is to be expected for the Vajjians not decline.
dn16:1.4.9: Have you heard, Ānanda: ‘The Vajjians do not establish (new) laws that were not established, (or) cut off (old) laws that were established, and carry on with such laws as were accepted in the Ancient Vajjian Constitution?’”
dn16:1.4.10: “I have heard this, reverend Sir: ‘The Vajjians do not establish (new) laws that were not established, (or) cut off (old) laws that were established, and they carry on with such laws as were accepted in the Ancient Vajjian Constitution.’”
dn16:1.4.11: “For as long, Ānanda, as the Vajjians do not establish (new) laws that were not established, (or) cut off (old) laws that were established, and they carry on with such laws as were accepted in the Ancient Vajjian Constitution surely growth, Ānanda, is to be expected for the Vajjians not decline.
dn16:1.4.12: Have you heard, Ānanda: ‘The Vajjians honour the elders of the Vajjians, respect, revere, worship and think them worth listening to?’”
dn16:1.4.13: “I have heard this, reverend Sir: ‘The Vajjians honour the elders of the Vajjians, respect, revere, worship and think them worth listening to.’”
dn16:1.4.14: “For as long, Ānanda, as the Vajjians will honour the elders of the Vajjians, respect, revere, worship and think them worth listening to, surely growth, Ānanda, is to be expected for the Vajjians not decline.
dn16:1.4.15: Have you heard, Ānanda: ‘The Vajjians do not coerce and force their women and girls to dwell (with them) against their will?’”
dn16:1.4.16: “I have heard this, reverend Sir: ‘The Vajjians do not coerce and force their women and girls to dwell (with them) against their will.’”
dn16:1.4.17: “For as long, Ānanda, as the Vajjians will not coerce and force their women and girls to dwell (with them) against their will, surely growth, Ānanda, is to be expected for the Vajjians not decline.
dn16:1.4.18: Have you heard, Ānanda: * ‘The Vajjians honour the Vajjian shrines amongst the Vajjians, both within and without (the city), respect, revere, and worship (them), and do not allow the righteous sacrifices that were formerly given, formerly made, to be neglected?’”
dn16:1.4.19: “I have heard this, reverend Sir: * ‘The Vajjians honour the Vajjian shrines amongst the Vajjians, both within and without (the city), respect, revere, and worship (them), and do not allow the righteous sacrifices that were formerly given, formerly made, to be neglected.”
dn16:1.4.20: “For as long, Ānanda, * as the Vajjians will honour the Vajjian shrines amongst the Vajjians, both within and without (the city), respect, revere, and worship (them), and do not allow the righteous sacrifices that were formerly given, formerly made, to be neglected surely growth, Ānanda, is to be expected for the Vajjians not decline.
dn16:1.4.21: Have you heard, Ānanda: ‘The Vajjians have made good arrangements in regard to the lawful protection, safety, and guarding of the Worthy Ones, so that Worthy Ones in the future can enter the realm, and having entered the Worthy Ones can live comfortably in the realm?”
dn16:1.4.22: “I have heard this, reverend Sir: ‘The Vajjians have made good arrangements in regard to the lawful protection, safety, and guarding of the Worthy Ones, and that the Worthy Ones in the future can enter the realm, and having entered the Worthy Ones can live comfortably in the realm.”
dn16:1.4.23: “For as long, Ānanda, as the Vajjians will make good arrangements in regard to the lawful protection, safety, and guarding of the Worthy Ones, and that the Worthy Ones in the future can enter the realm, and having entered, the Worthy Ones can live comfortably in the realm, surely growth, Ānanda, is to be expected for the Vajjians not decline.”
dn16:1.5.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed the Magadhan chief minister the brahmin Vassakāra, (saying):
dn16:1.5.2: “At one time, brahmin, I was living near Vesālī near to the Sārandada Shrine
dn16:1.5.3: and there I taught the Vajjians these seven things which prevent decline.
dn16:1.5.4: For as long, brahmin, as the Vajjians maintain these seven things which prevent decline, and the Vajjians agree with these seven things which prevent decline, surely growth, brahmin, is to be expected for the Vajjians not decline.”
dn16:1.5.5: After this was said, the Magadhan chief minister the brahmin Vassakāra addressed the Fortunate One, (saying):
dn16:1.5.6: “If the Vajjians, dear Gotama, were endowed with even one or the other of these seven things which prevent decline, surely growth is to be expected not decline,
dn16:1.5.7: what to say about having seven things which prevent decline?
dn16:1.5.8: The Vajjians cannot be overcome, dear Gotama, by the Magadhan King Ajātasattu, the son of Lady Wisdom, by war, but only through diplomacy, or through the breaking of the alliance.
dn16:1.5.9: And now, dear Gotama, we shall go, as we have many duties, and there is much which ought to be done.”
dn16:1.5.10: “Now is the time, brahmin, for whatever you are thinking.”
dn16:1.5.11: Then the Magadhan chief minister the brahmin Vassakāra, after greatly rejoicing and gladly receiving this word of the Fortunate One, rose from his seat and departed.
dn16:1.6.1: Then the Fortunate One, not long after the Magadhan chief minister, the brahmin Vassakāra, had gone, addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:1.6.2: “Go, Ānanda, and whatever monks there are living in dependence on Rājagaha, assemble them in the Attendance Hall.”
dn16:1.6.3: “Very well, reverend Sir,” said venerable Ānanda, and after replying to the Fortunate One, * and assembling whatever monks there were living in dependence on Rājagaha in the Attendance Hall, he approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he stood on one side. While standing on one side venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:1.6.4: “The Community of monks have assembled, reverend Sir, now is the time, Fortunate One, for whatever you are thinking.”
dn16:1.6.5: Then the Fortunate One after rising from his seat approached the Attendance Hall, and after approaching he sat down on the prepared seat.
dn16:1.6.6: While sitting the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
dn16:1.6.7: “I will teach you seven things which prevent decline,
dn16:1.6.8: listen to it, apply your minds well, and I will speak.”
dn16:1.6.9: “Very well, reverend Sir,” those monks replied to the Fortunate One,
dn16:1.6.10: and the Fortunate One said this:
dn16:1.6.11: “For as long, monks, as the monks will assemble regularly and assemble frequently, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.6.12: For as long, monks, as the monks will assemble unanimously, rise unanimously, and carry out their Community duties unanimously, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.6.13: For as long, monks, as the monks do not establish (new) laws that were not established, (or) cut off (old) laws that were established, and they carry on with such training-rules as have been accepted, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.6.14: * For as long, monks, as the monks will honour the elder monks, those of long-standing, a long time gone-forth, the Fathers of the Community, the Leaders of the Community, respect, revere, worship and think them worth listening to, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.6.15: For as long, monks, as the monks will not come under the influence of craving which has arisen for continued existence, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.6.16: For as long, monks, as the monks will have desire for forest dwellings, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.6.17: For as long, monks, as the monks individually will attend to the ways of mindfulness, so that their fellow celibates, who are well-behaved, in the future can come, and having come to their fellow celibates, who are well-behaved, can live comfortably, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.6.18: For as long, monks, as the monks will maintain these seven things which prevent decline, and the monks will agree with these seven things which prevent decline, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.7.1: I will teach you a further seven things which prevent decline, listen to it, apply your minds well, and I will speak.”
dn16:1.7.2: “Very well, reverend Sir,” those monks replied to the Fortunate One,
dn16:1.7.3: and the Fortunate One said this:
dn16:1.7.4: * “For as long, monks, as the monks are not devoted to the pleasure in work, the delight in work, and are not attached to work, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.7.5: For as long, monks, as the monks are not devoted to the pleasure in speech, the delight in speech, and are not attached to speech, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.7.6: For as long, monks, as the monks are not devoted to the pleasure in sleep, the delight in sleep, and are not attached to sleep, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.7.7: For as long, monks, as the monks are not devoted to the pleasure of company, the delight in company, and are not attached to company, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.7.8: For as long, monks, as the monks do not have evil wishes, do not go under the influence of evil wishes, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.7.9: For as long, monks, as the monks do not have wicked friends, do not have wicked companions, do not have wicked comrades, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.7.10: For as long, monks, as the monks do not achieve only mundane or incomplete attainment, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.8.1: For as long, monks, as the monks will maintain these seven things which prevent decline, and the monks will agree with these seven things which prevent decline, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.8.2: I will teach you a further seven things which prevent decline, listen to it, apply your minds well, and I will speak.” “Very well, reverend Sir,” those monks replied to the Fortunate One, and the Fortunate One said this:
dn16:1.8.3: “For as long, monks, as the monks will have faith, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.8.4: For as long, monks, as the monks will have a conscientious mind, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.8.5: For as long, monks, as the monks will have a sense of shame, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.8.6: For as long, monks, as the monks will be learned, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.8.7: For as long, monks, as the monks will be strenuous, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.8.8: For as long, monks, as the monks will attend to mindfulness,
dn16:1.8.9: surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline. For as long, monks, as the monks will possess wisdom, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.8.10: For as long, monks, as the monks will maintain these seven things which prevent decline, and the monks will agree with these seven things which prevent decline, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.8.11: I will teach you a further seven things which prevent decline, listen to it, apply your minds well, and I will speak.”
dn16:1.8.12: “Very well, reverend Sir,” those monks replied to the Fortunate One,
dn16:1.8.13: and the Fortunate One said this:
dn16:1.9.1: “For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the factor of Perfect Awakening that is Mindfulness, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.9.2: For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the factor of Perfect Awakening that is Investigation of (the nature of) things, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.9.3: For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the factor of Perfect Awakening that is Energy, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.9.4: For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the factor of Perfect Awakening that is Rapture, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.9.5: For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the factor of Perfect Awakening that is Calm, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.9.6: For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the factor of Perfect Awakening that is Concentration,
dn16:1.9.7: surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline. For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the factor of Perfect Awakening that is Equanimity, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.10.1: For as long, monks, as the monks will maintain these seven things which prevent decline, and the monks will agree with these seven things which prevent decline, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.10.2: I will teach you a further seven things which prevent decline, listen to it, apply your minds well, and I will speak.”
dn16:1.10.3: “Very well, reverend Sir,” those monks replied to the Fortunate One,
dn16:1.10.4: and the Fortunate One said this:
dn16:1.10.5: “For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the perception of impermanence, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.10.6: For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the perception of non-self, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.10.7: For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the perception of the unattractive, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.10.8: For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the perception of danger, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.10.9: For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the perception of giving up, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.10.10: For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the perception of dispassion,
dn16:1.10.11: surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline. For as long, monks, as the monks will develop the perception of cessation, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.10.12: For as long, monks, as the monks will maintain these seven things which prevent decline, and the monks will agree with these seven things which prevent decline, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline. I will teach you a further six things which prevent decline,
dn16:1.11.1: listen to it, apply your minds well, and I will speak.”
dn16:1.11.2: “Very well, reverend Sir,” those monks replied to the Fortunate One,
dn16:1.11.3: and the Fortunate One said this:
dn16:1.11.4: “For as long, monks, as the monks with friendly actions by way of the body will serve (their) fellow celibates, both in public and in private, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.11.5: For as long, monks, as the monks with friendly actions by way of speech will serve
dn16:1.11.6: (their) fellow celibates, both in public and in private, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline. For as long, monks, as the monks with friendly actions by way of the mind will serve (their) fellow celibates, both in public and in private, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.11.7: For as long, monks, as the monks (in regard to) those righteous gains, received in accordance with the Teaching - whatever amount has been received in the bowl - will divide and share such gains with those who are virtuous, fellow celibates, and share (them) in common, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.11.8: For as long, monks, as the monks (are endowed with) those virtues which are unbroken, faultless, unspotted, unblemished, productive of freedom, praised by the wise, not clung to, leading to concentration, (and) will live endowed with virtue amongst their fellow celibates who (themselves) possess such virtue, both in public and in private, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.11.9: For as long, monks, as the monks (are endowed with) that which is Ariyan View, which leads out, which leads to the complete destruction of suffering for one who acts thus, (and) will live endowed with (Right) View amongst those who (themselves) possess such (Right) View, both in public and in private, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
dn16:1.11.10: For as long, monks, as the monks will maintain these six things which prevent decline, and the monks will agree with these six things which prevent decline, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.”
dn16:1.12.1: There also the Fortunate One, while living near Rājagaha on the Vultures’ Peak Mountain, spoke frequently to the monks about the Teaching, (saying):
dn16:1.12.2: “Such is virtue, such is concentration, such is wisdom,
dn16:1.12.3: when virtue is well-developed it yields great fruit and brings great advantages in regard to concentration,
dn16:1.12.4: when concentration is well-developed it yields great fruit and brings great advantages in regard to wisdom,
dn16:1.12.5: when wisdom is well-developed the mind is completely liberated from the pollutants,
dn16:1.12.6: that is to say: the pollutant of sensuality, the pollutant of (craving for) continued existence, the pollutant of ignorance.”
dn16:1.13.1: Then the Fortunate One, after living near Rājagaha for as long as he liked, addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:1.13.3: “Very well, reverend Sir,” venerable Ānanda replied to the Fortunate One.
dn16:1.13.4: Then the Fortunate One together with a great Community of monks arrived at Ambalaṭṭhikā.
dn16:1.14.1: There the Fortunate One lived near Ambalaṭṭhikā in the King’s Rest House.
dn16:1.14.2: There also the Fortunate One, while living in Ambalaṭṭhikā in the King’s Rest House, spoke frequently to the monks about the Teaching, (saying):
dn16:1.14.3: “Such is virtue, such is concentration, such is wisdom,
dn16:1.14.4: when virtue is well-developed it yields great fruit and brings great advantages in regard to concentration,
dn16:1.14.5: when concentration is well-developed it yields great fruit and brings great advantages in regard to wisdom,
dn16:1.14.6: when wisdom is well-developed the mind is completely liberated from the pollutants,
dn16:1.14.7: that is to say: the pollutant of sensuality, the pollutant of (craving for) continued existence, the pollutant of ignorance.”
dn16:1.15.1: Then the Fortunate One, after living near Ambalaṭṭhikā for as long as he liked, addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:1.15.3: “Very well, reverend Sir,” venerable Ānanda replied to the Fortunate One.
dn16:1.15.4: Then the Fortunate One together with a great Community of monks arrived at Nāḷandā.
dn16:1.15.5: There the Fortunate One lived near Nāḷanda in Pāvārika’s Mango Wood.
dn16:1.16.1: Then venerable Sāriputta approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side venerable Sāriputta said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:1.16.2: “I have confidence, reverend Sir, in the Fortunate One in this way:
dn16:1.16.3: that neither in the past, the future, or at present is there found another ascetic or brahmin who has more deep knowledge in regard to Perfect Awakening than the Fortunate One.”
dn16:1.16.4: “You have spoken this great and imposing speech, Sāriputta, a definite, (well-)grasped, lion’s roar that was roared, (saying):
dn16:1.16.5: ‘I have confidence, reverend Sir, in the Fortunate One in this way:
dn16:1.16.6: that neither in the past, the future, or at present is there found another ascetic or brahmin who has more deep knowledge in regard to Perfect Awakening than the Fortunate One.’
dn16:1.16.7: * But have you, Sāriputta, understood those who, in past times, were Worthy and Perfect Sambuddhas, and known with your mind the minds of those Fortunate Ones?
dn16:1.16.8: (Or that) those Fortunate Ones had such and such virtues, those Fortunate Ones had such and such qualities, those Fortunate Ones had such and such wisdom, those Fortunate Ones had such and such lifestyles, those Fortunate Ones had such and such liberations?”
dn16:1.16.10: “But have you, Sāriputta, * understood those who, in the future times, will be Worthy and Perfect Sambuddhas, and known with your mind the minds of those Fortunate Ones?
dn16:1.16.11: (Or that) those Fortunate Ones will have such and such virtues, those Fortunate Ones will have such and such qualities, those Fortunate Ones will have such and such wisdom, those Fortunate Ones will have such and such lifestyles, those Fortunate Ones will have such and such liberations?”
dn16:1.16.13: * “But have you understood I, who am, at present, a Worthy and Perfect Sambuddha, and known with your mind (my) mind?
dn16:1.16.14: (Or that) the Fortunate One has such and such virtues, the Fortunate One has such and such qualities, the Fortunate One has such and such wisdom, the Fortunate One has such and such a lifestyle, the Fortunate One has such and such a liberation?”
dn16:1.16.16: “Here then, Sāriputta, in regard to those past, future, and present Worthy and Perfect Sambuddhas you have no full and exact knowledge with (your own) mind.
dn16:1.16.17: Then how is it, Sāriputta, at present that you have spoken (such) a great and imposing speech, a definite, (well-)grasped, lion’s roar that was roared, (saying):
dn16:1.16.18: ‘I have confidence, reverend Sir, in the Fortunate One in this way: that neither in the past, the future, or at present is there found another ascetic or brahmin who has more deep knowledge in regard to Perfect Awakening than the Fortunate One'?”
dn16:1.17.1: “I do not, reverend Sir, in regard to those past, future, and present Worthy and Perfect Sambuddhas have full and exact knowledge with (my own) mind.
dn16:1.17.2: However, I understand (what I said) is in conformity with the Teaching.
dn16:1.17.3: It is like a King’s city, reverend Sir, near the border areas, having strong foundations, strong walls and gateways, and a single door,
dn16:1.17.4: and there is a watchman, wise, accomplished, and intelligent, warding off those unknown, and letting through those well-known.
dn16:1.17.5: While going around the road on inspection through the whole of that city he may not see (such) fissures in the wall or openings in the wall that even a cat could go out through,
dn16:1.17.7: (but he knows): ‘Whatever grosser beings enter or depart from this city all of them surely enter or depart through this door.’
dn16:1.17.8: Similarly, reverend Sir, I understand it is in conformity with the Teaching,
dn16:1.17.9: that whoever, reverend Sir, in the past times, are Worthy Ones, Perfect Sambuddhas, all those Fortunate Ones, after giving up the five hindrances, have penetrated with wisdom the corruptions of the mind that make one feeble, have established their minds in the four ways of attending to mindfulness, and after developing just as it is the Seven Factors of Awakening, have awakened to the unsurpassed and Perfect Awakening.
dn16:1.17.10: That whoever, reverend Sir, in the future times, are Worthy Ones, Perfect Sambuddhas all those Fortunate Ones, after giving up the five hindrances, and penetrating with wisdom the corruptions of the mind that make one feeble, and establishing their minds in the four ways of attending to mindfulness, and developing just as it is the Seven Factors of Awakening, will awaken to the unsurpassed and Perfect Awakening.

dn16:1.20.4: The Fortunate One consented by maintaining silence.

While standing on one side, the laymen of Pāṭaligāma said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:1.21.2: “The rest house is spread with mats all over, reverend Sir, the seats are prepared, the water-pot is set up, and the oil-lamp is lit,
dn16:1.21.3: now is the time, reverend Sir, for whatever the Fortunate One is thinking.”
dn16:1.22.1: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the evening time, after picking up his bowl and robe, together with the Community of monks, approached the rest house, and after approaching, washing his feet, and entering the rest house, he sat down near to the middle pillar, facing the East,
dn16:1.22.2: and the Community of monks, after washing their feet, and entering the rest house, sat down (behind the Fortunate One) near the West wall, facing the East,

dn16:1.25.1: * Then the Fortunate One, after instructing, rousing, enthusing, and cheering the laymen of Pāṭaligāma for most of the night with a talk about the Teaching, dismissed them, (saying):

dn16:1.25.3: “Very well, reverend Sir,” said those laymen of Pāṭaligāma, and after replying to the Fortunate One, rising from their seats, worshipping and circumambulating the Fortunate One, went away.

dn16:1.26.1: Now at that time the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra were building up a city at Pāṭaligāma to ward off the Vajjians. Then at that time a great many Divinities, thousands upon thousands,
dn16:1.26.2: were taking possession of grounds at Pāṭaligāma.
dn16:1.26.3: In that place where the great Divinities took possession of grounds, there the powerful rulers and great royal ministers’ minds inclined to building up residences.
dn16:1.27.1: In that place where the middling Divinities took possession of grounds, there the middling rulers and middling royal ministers’ minds inclined to building up residences.
dn16:1.27.2: In that place where the lower Divinities took possession of grounds, there the lower rulers and lower royal ministers’ minds inclined to building up residences.
dn16:1.27.3: The Fortunate One saw with his Divine-eye, which is purified, and surpasses that of (normal) men, that those Divinities, thousands upon thousands, were taking possession of grounds at Pāṭaligāma.
dn16:1.27.4: Then towards the time of dawn, having risen from his seat, the Fortunate One addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:1.27.5: “Now who, Ānanda, is building a city at Pāṭaligāma?”
dn16:1.27.6: “The Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra, reverend Sir, are building up a city at Pāṭaligāma to ward off the Vajjians.”
dn16:1.28.1: “It is just as though, Ānanda, (they are building) after consulting with the Tāvatiṁsa Divinities,
dn16:1.28.2: so, Ānanda, are the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra building up a city at Pāṭaligāma to ward off the Vajjians.
dn16:1.28.3: Here, Ānanda, I saw with my Divine-eye, which is purified, and surpasses that of (normal) men, that a great many Divinities, thousands upon thousands, were taking possession of grounds at Pāṭaligāma.
dn16:1.28.4: In that place where the great Divinities took possession of grounds, there the powerful rulers and great royal ministers’ minds inclined to building up residences.
dn16:1.28.5: In that place where the middling Divinities took possession of grounds, there the middling rulers and middling royal ministers’ minds inclined to building up residences.
dn16:1.28.6: In that place where the lower Divinities took possession of grounds, there the lower rulers and lower royal ministers’ minds inclined to building up residences.
dn16:1.28.7: For as long, Ānanda, as there is an Ariyan sphere (of influence), for as long as there is trade, this basket-opening Pāṭaliputta will be the chief city.
dn16:1.28.8: For Pāṭaliputta, Ānanda, there will be three dangers:
dn16:1.28.9: from fire and from water and from the breaking of an alliance.”
dn16:1.29.1: Then the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching, they exchanged greetings with the Fortunate One,

dn16:2.7.1: “The monk Sāḷha, Ānanda, through the destruction of the pollutants, without pollutants, freed in mind, freed through wisdom, dwelt having known, having directly experienced, and having attained (Nibbāna) himself in this very life.

dn16:2.8.1: But it is not such a wonder, Ānanda, that those who have become human should die,
dn16:2.8.2: but if (every time) there is a death in this place, after approaching the Realised One, you were to ask about it, Ānanda, that would be troublesome to the Realised One.
dn16:2.8.3: Therefore, Ānanda, I will teach (this) presentation of the Teaching called the Mirror of (the True Nature of) Things, endowed with which a Noble Disciple desiring to do so may declare about himself:
dn16:2.8.4: ‘Exhausted is (birth in) Hell, exhausted is (birth in) an animal’s womb, exhausted is (birth in) the realm of the Fallen Spirits, exhausted is falling into an unhappy destiny in the lower realms, I am a Stream-Enterer, no longer subject to falling (into the lower realms), and have a fixed destiny ending in Final Awakening.’
dn16:2.9.1: And what, Ānanda, is (this) presentation of the Teaching called the Mirror of (the True Nature of) Things, endowed with which a Noble Disciple desiring to do so may declare about himself:
dn16:2.9.2: ‘Exhausted is (birth in) Hell, exhausted is (birth in) an animal’s womb, exhausted is (birth in) the realm of the Fallen Spirits, exhausted is falling into an unhappy destiny in the lower realms, I am a Stream-Enterer, no longer subject to falling (into the lower realms), and have a fixed destiny ending in Final Awakening'?

dn16:2.9.4: ‘Such is he, the Fortunate One, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha, the one endowed with understanding and good conduct, the Happy One, the One who understands the worlds, the unsurpassed guide for those people who need taming, the Teacher of Divinities and men, the Buddha, the Fortunate One.’
dn16:2.9.5: He is endowed with perfect confidence in the Teaching (thinking):
dn16:2.9.6: ‘The Teaching has been well-proclaimed by the Fortunate One, it is visible, not subject to time, inviting inspection, onward leading, and can be understood by the wise for themselves.’
dn16:2.9.7: He is endowed with perfect confidence in the Community (thinking):
dn16:2.9.8: ‘The Fortunate One’s Community of disciples are good in their practice, the Fortunate One’s Community of disciples are straight in their practice, the Fortunate One’s Community of disciples are systematic in their practice, the Fortunate One’s Community of disciples are correct in their practice, that is to say, the four pairs of persons, the eight individual persons, this is the Fortunate One’s Community of disciples, they are worthy of offerings, of hospitality, of gifts, and of reverential salutation, they are an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’

dn16:2.11.3: “Very well, reverend Sir,” venerable Ānanda replied to the Fortunate One.

dn16:2.11.5: There the Fortunate One lived near Vesālī in Ambapālī’s Wood.
dn16:2.12.1: There the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
dn16:2.12.2: “Mindfully and with full awareness, monks, a monk should live,
dn16:2.12.3: this is our advice to you.
dn16:2.12.4: And how, monks, is a monk mindful?
dn16:2.12.5: Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating (the nature of) the body in the body, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, after removing avarice and sorrow regarding the world;
dn16:2.12.6: he dwells contemplating (the nature of) feelings in feelings, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, after removing avarice and sorrow regarding the world;
dn16:2.12.7: he dwells contemplating (the nature of) the mind in the mind,
dn16:2.12.8: ardent, fully aware, and mindful, after removing avarice and sorrow regarding the world; he dwells contemplating (the nature of) things in (various) things, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, after removing avarice and sorrow regarding the world.
dn16:2.12.9: Thus, monks, a monk is mindful.
dn16:2.13.1: And how, monks, does a monk have full awareness?
dn16:2.13.2: Here, monks, a monk in going forwards, in going back, is one who practises with full awareness, in looking ahead, or in looking around, he is one who practises with full awareness, in bending or in stretching, he is one who practises with full awareness, in bearing his double-robe, bowl, and (other) robes, he is one who practises with full awareness, in eating, in drinking, in chewing, in tasting, he is one who practises with full awareness, in passing stool and urine, he is one who practises with full awareness, in going, in standing, in sitting, in sleeping, in waking, in talking, and in maintaining silence, he is one who practises with full awareness.
dn16:2.13.3: Thus, monks, a monk has full awareness.
dn16:2.13.4: Mindfully and with full awareness, monks, a monk should live,
dn16:2.13.5: this is our advice to you.”
dn16:2.14.0: The courtesan Ambapālī heard: “The Fortunate One, it seems, has reached Vesālī
dn16:2.14.1: and is living near Vesālī in my Mango Wood.”
dn16:2.14.2: Then the courtesan Ambapālī, after having (many) great and august vehicles prepared, and mounting (those) great and august vehicles, departed with those great and august vehicles from Vesālī, and after approaching by vehicle to her pleasure garden as far as the ground for vehicles (would allow),
dn16:2.14.3: and descending from the vehicles, she approached the Fortunate One by foot, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, she sat down on one side.
dn16:2.14.4: * While the courtesan Ambapālī was sitting on one side the Fortunate One instructed, roused, enthused, and cheered her with a talk about the Teaching.
dn16:2.14.5: Then the courtesan Ambapālī, having been instructed, roused, enthused, and cheered by the Fortunate One with a talk about the Teaching, said to the Fortunate One:
dn16:2.14.6: “May the Fortunate One consent, reverend Sir, to me (offering him) a meal on the morrow, together with the Community of monks.”
dn16:2.14.7: The Fortunate One consented by maintaining silence.
dn16:2.14.8: Then the courtesan Ambapālī, having understood the Fortunate One’s consent, after rising from her seat, worshipping and circumambulating the Fortunate One, went away.
dn16:2.15.1: The Licchavīs from Vesālī heard: “The Fortunate One, it seems, had reached Vesālī and is living near Vesālī in Ambapālī’s Wood.”
dn16:2.15.2: Then those Licchavīs, after having (many) great and august vehicles prepared, and mounting (those) great and august vehicles, departed with those great and august vehicles from Vesālī.
dn16:2.15.3: There some of the Licchavīs were blue, having a blue appearance, with blue clothes and blue decorations, some of the Licchavīs were yellow, having a yellow appearance, with yellow clothes and yellow decorations, some of the Licchavīs were red, having a red appearance, with red clothes and red decorations, some of the Licchavīs were white, having a white appearance, with white clothes and white decorations.
dn16:2.16.1: Then the courtesan Ambapālī rolled alongside the Licchavī youths axle by axle, wheel by wheel, and yoke by yoke.
dn16:2.16.2: Then those Licchavīs said this to the courtesan Ambapālī:
dn16:2.16.3: “Why do you, Ambapālī, roll alongside the Licchavī youths axle by axle, wheel by wheel, and yoke by yoke?”
dn16:2.16.4: “Because I have invited the Fortunate One, noble sirs, for a meal on the morrow, together with the Community of monks.”
dn16:2.16.5: “Give (us) this meal, Ambapālī, for a hundred thousand (kahapanas).”
dn16:2.16.6: “If, noble sirs, you would give Vesālī and its revenues still I would not give this meal (to you).”
dn16:2.16.7: Then the Licchavīs snapped their fingers, (thinking):
dn16:2.16.8: “We have surely been defeated by a woman, we have surely been defeated by a woman.”
dn16:2.16.9: Then the Licchavīs entered Ambapālī’s Wood.
dn16:2.17.1: The Fortunate One saw those Licchavīs coming from afar,
dn16:2.17.2: and having seen (them), he addressed the monks, (saying):
dn16:2.17.3: * “Let those monks who have not seen the Tāvatiṁsa Divinities, monks,
dn16:2.17.4: look at the Licchavī troupe, monks,
dn16:2.17.5: look upon the Licchavī troupe, monks,
dn16:2.17.6: contemplate the Licchavī troupe, monks, who are like the Tāvatiṁsa (Divinities).”
dn16:2.18.1: Then after the Licchavīs had gone as far as the ground for vehicles (would allow), and had descended from the vehicles, they approached the Fortunate One by foot, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, they sat down at one side.
dn16:2.18.2: * While the Licchavīs were sitting on one side the Fortunate One instructed, roused, enthused, and cheered them with a talk about the Teaching.
dn16:2.18.3: Then the Licchavīs, having been instructed, roused, enthused, and cheered by the Fortunate One with a talk about the Teaching, said to the Fortunate One:
dn16:2.18.4: “Please consent to us (offering) a meal on the morrow, together with the Community of monks.”
dn16:2.18.6: “I have (already) consented to the courtesan Ambapālī’s meal on the morrow.”
dn16:2.18.7: Then the Licchavīs snapped their fingers, (thinking):
dn16:2.18.8: “We have surely been defeated by a woman, we have surely been defeated by a woman.”
dn16:2.18.9: Then the Licchavīs, after greatly rejoicing and gladly receiving this word of the Fortunate One, rising from their seats, worshipping and circumambulating the Fortunate One, went away.
dn16:2.19.1: Then the courtesan Ambapālī after the night had passed, having had excellent foodstuffs made ready in her own pleasure park, had the time announced to the Fortunate One,
dn16:2.19.2: (saying): “It is time, reverend Sir, the meal is ready.”
dn16:2.19.3: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, together with the Community of monks, approached the courtesan Ambapālī’s residence, and after approaching he sat down on the prepared seat.
dn16:2.19.4: Then the courtesan Ambapālī with her own hand served and satisfied the Community of monks with the Buddha at its head with excellent foodstuffs.
dn16:2.19.5: Then the courtesan Ambapālī, when the Fortunate One had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, having taken a certain low seat, sat down on one side.
dn16:2.19.6: While sitting on one side the courtesan Ambapālī said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:2.19.7: “I donate this pleasure park, reverend Sir, to the Community of monks with the Buddha at its head.”
dn16:2.19.8: The Fortunate One accepted the pleasure park.
dn16:2.19.9: * Then the Fortunate One, after instructing, rousing, enthusing, and cheering the courtesan Ambapālī with a talk about the Teaching, having risen from the seat, went away.
dn16:2.20.1: There also the Fortunate One, while living in Vesālī in Ambapālī’s Wood, spoke frequently to the monks about the Teaching, (saying):
dn16:2.20.2: “Such is virtue, such is concentration, such is wisdom,
dn16:2.20.3: when virtue is well-developed it yields great fruit and brings great advantages in regard to concentration,
dn16:2.20.4: when concentration is well-developed it yields great fruit and brings great advantages in regard to wisdom,
dn16:2.20.5: when wisdom is well-developed the mind is completely liberated from the pollutants,
dn16:2.20.6: that is to say: the pollutant of sensuality, the pollutant of (craving for) continued existence, the pollutant of ignorance.”
dn16:2.21.1: Then the Fortunate One, after living near Ambapālī’s Wood for as long as he liked, addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:2.21.2: “Come Ānanda let us approach the little village of Beluva.”
dn16:2.21.3: “Very well, reverend Sir,” venerable Ānanda replied to the Fortunate One.
dn16:2.21.4: Then the Fortunate One together with a great Community of monks arrived at the little village of Beluva.
dn16:2.21.5: There the Fortunate One lived near the little village of Beluva.
dn16:2.22.1: There the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
dn16:2.22.2: * “Go, monks, and undertake the Rains Retreat in the vicinity of Vesālī (living) like friends, like companions, like comrades,
dn16:2.22.3: and I will spend the Rains Retreat right here at the little village of Beluva.”
dn16:2.22.4: “Very well, reverend Sir,” and those monks, * after replying to the Fortunate One, undertook the Rains Retreat in the vicinity of Vesālī (living) like friends, like companions, like comrades.
dn16:2.22.5: But the Fortunate One spent the Rains Retreat right there at the little village of Beluva.
dn16:2.23.1: Then while dwelling for the Rains Retreat, a heavy affliction arose for the Fortunate One, and continued with strong and death-like feelings.
dn16:2.23.2: There the Fortunate One dwelt mindfully, with full awareness, and without being troubled.
dn16:2.23.3: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
dn16:2.23.4: “It is not suitable that I, without having addressed my attendants, without having given notice to the Community of monks, should attain Final Emancipation.
dn16:2.23.5: Having energetically dismissed this affliction, I could live on after determining the lifespan.”
dn16:2.24.1: Then the Fortunate One having energetically dismissed that affliction, lived on after determining the lifespan.
dn16:2.24.2: Then the Fortunate One’s affliction abated.
dn16:2.24.3: Then, the Fortunate One, having risen from that sickness, not long after rising, departed from the Sick Room and sat down on the prepared seat in front of that Room.
dn16:2.24.4: Then venerable Ānanda approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:2.24.5: “I have seen, reverend Sir, the Fortunate One comfortable, I have seen, reverend Sir, the Fortunate One bearing up (while sick), and my body, reverend Sir, became faint as it were, and although I could not see (straight), and things were not clear,
dn16:2.24.6: it appeared to me, reverend Sir, that the Fortunate One was sick, (but) it was some small comfort that the Fortunate One would not attain Final Emancipation
dn16:2.24.7: until the Fortunate One had spoken regarding the Community of monks.”
dn16:2.25.1: “But what, Ānanda, does the Community of monks expect of me?
dn16:2.25.2: The Teaching has been taught by me, Ānanda, without having made (a distinction between) esoteric and exoteric,
dn16:2.25.3: for the Realised One there is nothing, Ānanda, of a (closed) teacher’s fist in regard to the Teaching.
dn16:2.25.5: ‘I will lead the Community of monks’ or ‘I am the instructer of the Community of monks’ let him speak, Ānanda, regarding the Community of monks.
dn16:2.25.6: But to the Realised One, Ānanda, this (thought) does not occur:
dn16:2.25.7: ‘I will lead the Community of monks’ or ‘I am the instructor of the Community of monks’.
dn16:2.25.8: Then why, Ānanda, should the Realised One speak regarding the Community of monks?
dn16:2.25.9: I, Ānanda, at present, am old, elderly, of great age,
dn16:2.25.10: far gone, advanced in years, I am eighty years old.
dn16:2.25.11: It is like, Ānanda, an old cart, which (only) keeps going when shored up with bamboo,
dn16:2.25.12: just so, Ānanda, I think the Realised One’s body (only) keeps going when shored up with bamboo.
dn16:2.25.13: When the Realised One doesn't pay attention, Ānanda, to any of the signs, when all feelings have ceased, he lives having established the signless mind-concentration, and at that time, Ānanda, the Realised One’s body is most comfortable.
dn16:2.26.1: Therefore, Ānanda, live with yourself as an island, yourself as a refuge, with no other refuge, with the Teaching as an island, the Teaching as a refuge, with no other refuge.
dn16:2.26.2: And how, Ānanda, does a monk live with himself as an island, himself as a refuge, with no other refuge, with the Teaching as an island, the Teaching as a refuge, with no other refuge?
dn16:2.26.3: Here, Ānanda, a monk dwells contemplating (the nature of) the body in the body, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, after removing avarice and sorrow regarding the world;
dn16:2.26.4: he dwells contemplating (the nature of) feelings in feelings, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, after removing avarice and sorrow regarding the world;
dn16:2.26.5: he dwells contemplating (the nature of) the mind in the mind,
dn16:2.26.6: ardent, fully aware, and mindful, after removing avarice and sorrow regarding the world; he dwells contemplating (the nature of) things in (various) things, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, after removing avarice and sorrow regarding the world.
dn16:2.26.7: Thus, Ānanda, a monk lives with himself as an island, himself as a refuge, with no other refuge, with the Teaching as an island, the Teaching as a refuge, with no other refuge.
dn16:2.26.8: For whoever, Ānanda, whether at present or after my passing, lives with himself as an island, himself as a refuge, with no other refuge, with the Teaching as an island, the Teaching as a refuge, with no other refuge, those monks of mine, Ānanda, will go from darkness to the highest - whoever likes the training.”
dn16:2.26.9: The Second Chapter for Recital (is Finished).

dn16:3.12.7: What was the reason, reverend Sir, what was the cause, for the occurrence of this great earthquake?”
dn16:3.13.1: “There are these eight reasons, eight causes, Ānanda, for the occurrence of a great earthquake.
dn16:3.13.3: This great Earth, Ānanda, stands in the water, the water stands in the atmosphere, the atmosphere stands in space. There comes a time, Ānanda, when great winds blow, with the great winds blowing, the waters move, the waters having moved, the Earth moves.
dn16:3.13.4: This is the first reason, the first cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.
dn16:3.14.1: Furthermore, Ānanda, when an ascetic or a brahmin or a Divinity, one of great power, one of great majesty, has, through spiritual power, attained (complete) mastery of the mind, and has then developed even a trifling perception of the Earth, or an unlimited perception of water, this Earth moves, wavers, flutters, and shakes.
dn16:3.14.2: This is the second reason, the second cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.
dn16:3.15.1: Furthermore, Ānanda, when the Buddha-to-be falls away from the Tusita hosts, and mindfully, with full awareness, enters his mother’s womb, this Earth moves, wavers, flutters, and shakes.
dn16:3.15.2: This is the third reason, the third cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.
dn16:3.16.1: Furthermore, Ānanda, when the Buddha-to-be mindfully, with full awareness, exits his mother’s womb, this Earth moves, wavers, flutters, and shakes.
dn16:3.16.2: This is the fourth reason, the fourth cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.
dn16:3.17.1: Furthermore, Ānanda, when the Realised One perfectly awakens to the unsurpassed and Perfect Awakening, this Earth moves, wavers, flutters, and shakes.
dn16:3.17.2: This is the fifth reason, the fifth cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.
dn16:3.18.1: Furthermore, Ānanda, when the Realised One sets the unsurpassed wheel of the Teaching rolling, this Earth moves, wavers, flutters, and shakes.
dn16:3.18.2: This is the sixth reason, the sixth cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.
dn16:3.19.1: Furthermore, Ānanda, when the Realised One mindfully, with full awareness gives up the life-process, this Earth moves, wavers, flutters, and shakes.
dn16:3.19.2: This is the seventh reason, the seventh cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.
dn16:3.20.1: Furthermore, Ānanda, when the Realised One is Finally Emancipated in the Emancipation-element which has no basis for attachment remaining, this Earth moves, wavers, flutters, and shakes.
dn16:3.20.2: This is the eighth reason, the eighth cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.
dn16:3.20.3: These are the eight reasons, the eight causes, Ānanda, for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

dn16:3.24.1: There are, Ānanda, eight means of (mind) mastery.
dn16:3.25.1: Perceiving forms internally, someone sees forms externally, limited, beautiful or ugly,
dn16:3.25.2: and having mastered them, he is one who perceives thus: ‘I know, I see’.
dn16:3.25.3: This is the first means of (mind) mastery.
dn16:3.26.1: Perceiving forms internally, someone sees forms externally, unlimited, beautiful or ugly,
dn16:3.26.2: and having mastered them, he is one who perceives thus: ‘I know, I see’.
dn16:3.26.3: This is the second means of (mind) mastery.
dn16:3.27.1: Without perceiving forms internally, someone sees forms externally, limited, beautiful or ugly,
dn16:3.27.2: and having mastered them, he is one who perceives thus: ‘I know, I see’.
dn16:3.27.3: This is the third means of (mind) mastery.
dn16:3.28.1: Without perceiving forms internally, someone sees forms externally, unlimited, beautiful or ugly,
dn16:3.28.2: and having mastered them, he is one who perceives thus: ‘I know, I see’.
dn16:3.28.3: This is the fourth means of (mind) mastery.
dn16:3.29.1: Without perceiving forms internally, someone sees forms externally, blue, blue-coloured, of blue appearance, shiny blue,
dn16:3.29.2: just as the flower called Ummā is blue, blue-coloured, of blue appearance, shiny blue, or just as there is Banaras cloth smoothed on both sides that is blue, blue-coloured, of blue appearance, shiny blue,
dn16:3.29.3: so, without perceiving forms internally, someone sees forms externally, blue, blue-coloured, of blue appearance, shiny blue,
dn16:3.29.4: and having mastered them, he is one who perceives thus: ‘I know, I see’.
dn16:3.29.5: This is the fifth means of (mind) mastery.
dn16:3.30.1: Without perceiving forms internally, someone sees forms externally, yellow, yellow-coloured, of yellow appearance, shiny yellow,
dn16:3.30.2: just as the flower called Kaṇikāra is yellow, yellow-coloured, of yellow appearance, shiny yellow, or just as there is Banaras cloth smoothed on both sides that is yellow, yellow-coloured, of yellow appearance, shiny yellow,
dn16:3.30.3: so, without perceiving forms internally, someone sees forms externally, yellow, yellow colour, of yellow appearance, shiny yellow,
dn16:3.30.4: and having mastered them, he is one who perceives thus: ‘I know, I see’.
dn16:3.30.5: This is the sixth means of (mind) mastery.
dn16:3.31.1: Without perceiving forms internally, someone sees forms externally, red, red-coloured, of red appearance, shiny red,
dn16:3.31.2: just as the flower called Bandhujīvaka is red, red-coloured, of red appearance, shiny red, or just as there is Banaras cloth smoothed on both sides that is red, red-coloured, of red appearance, shiny red,
dn16:3.31.3: so, without perceiving forms internally, someone sees forms externally, red, red-coloured, of red appearance, shiny red,
dn16:3.31.4: and having mastered them, he is one who perceives thus: ‘I know, I see’.
dn16:3.31.5: This is the seventh means of (mind) mastery.
dn16:3.32.1: Without perceiving forms internally, someone sees forms externally, white, white-coloured, of white appearance, shiny white,
dn16:3.32.2: just as the Osadhī star, is white, white-coloured, of white appearance, shiny white, or just as there is Banaras cloth smoothed on both sides that is white, white-coloured, of white appearance, shiny white,
dn16:3.32.3: so, without perceiving forms internally, someone sees forms externally, white, white-coloured, of white appearance, shiny white,
dn16:3.32.4: and having mastered them, he is one who perceives thus: ‘I know, I see’.
dn16:3.32.5: This is the eighth means of (mind) mastery.
dn16:3.32.6: These, Ānanda, are the eight means of (mind) mastery.
dn16:3.33.5: Not perceiving forms internally, he sees forms externally.
dn16:3.33.9: Having completely transcended perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of (sensory) impact, not attending to perceptions of variety, (understanding): ‘This is endless space’, he abides in the sphere of endless space.
dn16:3.33.11: Having completely transcended the sphere of endless space, (understanding): ‘This is endless consciousness’, he abides in the sphere of endless consciousness.
dn16:3.33.13: Having completely transcended the sphere of endless consciousness, (understanding): ‘This is nothing’, he abides in the sphere of nothingness.
dn16:3.33.15: Having completely transcended the sphere of nothingness, he abides in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
dn16:3.33.17: Having completely transcended the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he abides in the cessation of perception and feeling.
dn16:3.33.19: These, Ānanda, are the eight liberations.

dn16:3.34.2: Then, Ānanda, the Wicked Māra approached me, and after approaching he stood on one side. While standing to one side, Ānanda, the Wicked Māra said this to me:
dn16:3.34.3: “May the Fortunate One attain Final Emancipation now, reverend Sir, may the Happy One attain Final Emancipation, now is the time, reverend Sir, for the Fortunate One’s Final Emancipation.”

dn16:3.40.6: “Then, Ānanda, there is this wrong-doing for you, there is this fault for you, in that you, despite such a gross hint being made by the Realised One, such a gross suggestion being made, was unable to penetrate it, and did not beg the Realised One, (saying):

dn16:3.47.1: and here today, Ānanda, at the Cāpāla Shrine I addressed you, (saying):
dn16:3.47.2: ‘Delightful, Ānanda, is Vesālī, delightful is the Udena Shrine, delightful is the Gotamaka Shrine, delightful is the Seven Mangos Shrine, delightful is the Many Sons Shrine, delightful is the Sārandada Shrine, delightful is the Cāpāla Shrine.
dn16:3.47.3: * Whoever has developed, Ānanda, made much of, carried on, established, maintained, augmented, and properly instigated the Four Paths to Power, could, if he wanted, remain for the lifespan or for what is left of the lifespan.
dn16:3.47.4: * The Realised One has developed, Ānanda, made much of, carried on, established, maintained, augmented, and properly instigated the Four Paths to Power. If he wanted, Ānanda, the Realised One could remain for the lifespan or for what is left of the lifespan.’
dn16:3.47.5: But despite such a gross hint, Ānanda, being made by the Realised One, such a gross suggestion being made, you were unable to penetrate it, and did not beg the Realised One, (saying):
dn16:3.47.6: ‘May the Fortunate One remain, reverend Sir, for the lifespan; may the Happy One remain for the lifespan, for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of Divinities and men.’
dn16:3.47.7: If you, Ānanda, had begged the Realised One twice the Realised One might have rejected your speech, but would have accepted it on the third occasion.
dn16:3.47.8: So, Ānanda, there is this wrong-doing for you, there is this fault for you.
dn16:3.48.1: Were you not warned by me when I declared:
dn16:3.48.2: ‘There is alteration in, separation from, and changeability in all that is dear and appealing’?
dn16:3.48.3: How can it be otherwise, Ānanda, for that which is obtained, born, become, conditioned, subject to dissolution? It is not possible (to say) this: ‘It should not dissolve’.
dn16:3.48.4: But this has been relinquished, cast out, let loose, abandoned by the Realised One, forsaken, the life-process that has been given up. For sure this word was spoken by the Realised One:
dn16:3.48.5: ‘Not long now there will be the Realised One’s Final Emancipation,
dn16:3.48.6: after the passing of three months the Realised One will attain Final Emancipation.’
dn16:3.48.7: The Realised One cannot for the sake of life go back on that, it is not possible.
dn16:3.48.8: Come Ānanda let us approach the Gabled House Hall in Great Wood.”
dn16:3.48.9: “Very well, reverend Sir,” venerable Ānanda replied to the Fortunate One.
dn16:3.49.1: * Then the Fortunate One with venerable Ānanda approached the Gabled House Hall in Great Wood, and after approaching he addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:3.49.2: “Go, Ānanda, and whatever monks are living in dependance on Vesālī assemble them in the Attendance Hall.”
dn16:3.49.3: “Very well, reverend Sir,” said venerable Ānanda, and after replying to the Fortunate One * and assembling whatever monks were living in dependance on Vesālī in the Attendance Hall, he approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he stood at one side. dn16:3.49.4: “The Community of monks has assembled, reverend Sir, now is the time, Fortunate One, for whatever you are thinking.”
dn16:3.50.1: Then the Fortunate One approached the Attendance Hall, and after approaching he sat down on the prepared seat.
dn16:3.50.2: While sitting the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
dn16:3.50.3: “Therefore, monks, whatever Teachings have, with deep knowledge, been taught by me, after grasping them well, you should practise, develop, and make a lot of them, so that the Spiritual Life may last long, and may endure for a long time, and that will be for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of Divinities and men.
dn16:3.50.4: And what are those Teachings that have, with deep knowledge, been taught by me, which after grasping them well, you should practise, develop, and make a lot of them, so that the Spiritual Life may last long, and may endure for a long time, that will be for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of Divinities and men? They are as follows:
dn16:3.50.5: The Four Ways of Attending to Mindfulness, the Four Right Strivings, the Four Paths to Power, the Five Faculties, the Five Strengths, the Seven Factors of Awakening, the Noble Eight-Fold Path.
dn16:3.51.1: These, monks, are those Teachings that have, with deep knowledge, been taught by me, after grasping them well, you should practise, develop, and make a lot of them, so that the Spiritual Life may last long, and may endure for a long time, and that will be for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of Divinities and men.”
dn16:3.51.2: Then the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):

dn16:4.15.2: The Fortunate One consented by maintaining silence.

dn16:4.17.2: (saying): “It is time, reverend Sir, the meal is ready.”

dn16:4.19.4: “Very well, reverend Sir”, said Cunda the Smith, and after replying to the Fortunate One, and throwing what was left over of that tender pork into a pit, he approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side.

dn16:4.26.1: Now at that time Pukkasa Mallaputta, a disciple of Āḷāra Kālāma, was travelling along the highway from Pāvā to Kusinārā.
dn16:4.26.2: Pukkasa Mallaputta saw the Fortunate One sitting at the root of a certain tree.
dn16:4.26.3: And having seen (him) he approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side Pukkasa Mallaputta said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:4.26.4: “It is wonderful, reverend Sir, it is marvellous, reverend Sir, that those who have gone forth, reverend Sir, live such a peaceful living.
dn16:4.27.1: Formerly, reverend Sir, Āḷāra Kālāma descended from the highway he was travelling along, and was dwelling for the day sat not far away at the root of a certain tree.
dn16:4.27.2: Then, reverend Sir, about five hundred wagons passed by very close to Āḷāra Kālāma.
dn16:4.27.3: Then, reverend Sir, a certain man who was traveling along behind those wagons approached Āḷāra Kālāma, and after approaching he said this to Āḷāra Kālāma:
dn16:4.27.4: ‘Did you not see, reverend Sir, about five hundred wagons pass by?’
dn16:4.27.6: ‘But, reverend Sir, did you not hear the sound?’
dn16:4.27.7: ‘I did not hear the sound, friend.’
dn16:4.27.12: ‘So you, reverend Sir, though conscious and awake, when about five hundred wagons passed by very close neither saw (them) nor heard a sound!
dn16:4.27.13: Why, reverend Sir, even your double-robe is covered with dust!’
dn16:4.27.15: Then this occurred to that man:
dn16:4.27.16: ‘Surely it is wonderful, surely it is marvellous, that those who have indeed gone forth live such a peaceful living.
dn16:4.27.17: Because though conscious and awake, when about five hundred wagons passed by very close he did not see (them) or hear a sound!’
dn16:4.27.18: And having gained great confidence in Āḷāra Kālāma, he left.”
dn16:4.28.2: which is the more difficult to do or the more difficult to come by:
dn16:4.28.3: that someone though conscious and awake, when about five hundred wagons passed by very close should neither see (them) nor hear a sound,
dn16:4.28.4: or that someone, though conscious and awake, when the Divinities rain down, when the Divinities throw it down, and the lightning flashes, and the thunder crashes forth, should neither see (it) nor hear a sound?”
dn16:4.29.1: “Why, reverend Sir, what to make of five-hundred wagons, six-hundred wagons, seven-hundred wagons, eight-hundred wagons, nine-hundred wagons, one thousand wagons, or one-hundred thousand wagons?
dn16:4.29.2: This is the more difficult to do or the more difficult to come by: that someone, though conscious and awake, when the Divinities rain down, when the Divinities throw it down, and the lightning flashes, and the thunder crashes forth, should neither see (it) nor hear a sound.”
dn16:4.30.1: “One day, Pukkusa, I was living near Ātumā at the Decorated House.
dn16:4.30.2: Now at that time the Divinities rained down, the Divinities threw it down, and the lightning flashed, and the thunder crashed forth, and not far away from the Decorated House two brothers who were farmers died, along with four oxen.
dn16:4.30.3: Then, Pukkusa, a great crowd of people having departed from Ātumā, went to the place where the brothers who were farmers and the four oxen had died.
dn16:4.31.1: Then, Pukkusa, at that time, after leaving the Decorated House, I was walking in the open air near the gate to the Decorated House.
dn16:4.31.2: Then, Pukkusa, a certain man from that crowd approached me, and after approaching and worshipping me, he stood on one side. While standing there, Pukkusa, I said to that man:
dn16:4.32.1: ‘Why, friend, has that great crowd of people assembled?’
dn16:4.32.2: ‘Just now, reverend Sir, the Divinities rained down, the Divinities threw it down, and the lightning flashed, and the thunder crashed forth, and two brothers who were farmers died, along with four oxen,
dn16:4.32.3: and that great crowd of people assembled here.
dn16:4.32.4: But where were you, reverend Sir?’
dn16:4.32.8: ‘But, reverend Sir, did you hear the sound?’
dn16:4.32.9: ‘I did not hear the sound, friend.’
dn16:4.32.14: ‘So, reverend Sir, though conscious and awake when the Divinities rained down, when the Divinities threw it down, and the lightning flashed, and the thunder crashed forth, you neither saw (it), nor heard a sound!’
dn16:4.33.1: Then, Pukkusa, this occurred to that man:
dn16:4.33.2: ‘Surely it is wonderful, surely it is marvellous, that those who have indeed gone forth live such a peaceful living.
dn16:4.33.3: Because though conscious and awake when the Divinities rained down, when the Divinities threw it down, and the lightning flashed, and the thunder crashed forth, he did not see (it) or hear a sound!’
dn16:4.33.4: And after gaining great confidence in me, worshipping and circumamblating me, he left.”
dn16:4.34.1: After this was said, Pukkusa Mallaputta said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:4.34.2: “That faith, reverend Sir, I have in Āḷāra Kālāma, I clear away as with a great wind, I wash (it) away as with a fast-flowing river:
dn16:4.34.3: Excellent, reverend Sir! Excellent, reverend Sir!
dn16:4.34.4: Just as, reverend Sir, one might set upright what has been overturned, or open up what has been closed, or show a path to one who is lost, or bear an oil lamp in the darkness so that one who has eyes can see forms, just so has the Teaching been made clear by the Fortunate One in more than one way.
dn16:4.34.5: I go to the Fortunate One, reverend Sir, for refuge, and to the Teaching, and to the Community of monks.
dn16:4.34.6: Please bear it in mind, Fortunate One, that I am a lay disciple who has gone for refuge from today forward for as long as I am furnished with life.”
dn16:4.35.1: Then Pukkusa Mallaputta addressed a certain man, (saying):
dn16:4.35.2: “Come, my man, bring me a pair of polished gold-coloured (robes), ready to wear.”
dn16:4.35.3: “Very well, reverend Sir,” said that man, and after replying to Pukkusa Mallaputta, he brought a pair of polished gold-coloured (robes), ready to wear.
dn16:4.35.4: Then Pukkusa Mallaputta offered that pair of polished gold-coloured (robes), ready to wear, to the Fortunate One, (saying):
dn16:4.35.5: * “Please accept, reverend Sir, this pair of polished gold-coloured (robes), ready to wear out of compassion for me, Fortunate One.”
dn16:4.35.6: “Then, Pukkusa, clothe me with one, and Ānanda with the other.”
dn16:4.35.7: “Very well, reverend Sir,” said Pukkusa Mallaputta, and after replying to the Fortunate One he clothed the Fortunate One with one, and Ānanda with the other.
dn16:4.36.1: * Then the Fortunate One instructed Pukkusa Mallaputta roused, enthused, and cheered (him) with a talk about the Teaching.
dn16:4.36.2: Then Pukkusa Mallaputta, having been instructed, roused, enthused, and cheered by the Fortunate One with a talk about the Teaching, after rising from his seat, worshipping and circumambulating the Fortunate One, departed.
dn16:4.37.1: Then, venerable Ānanda, not long after Pukkusa Mallaputta had departed, offered that pair of polished gold-coloured (robes), ready to wear, to the Fortunate One,
dn16:4.37.2: and when placed on the Fortunate One’s body they appeared to have lost their gleam.
dn16:4.37.3: Then venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:4.37.4: “It is wonderful, reverend Sir, it is marvellous, reverend Sir, how pure and clean is the Realised One’s skin-colour, reverend Sir!
dn16:4.37.5: This pair of polished gold-coloured (robes), ready to wear, reverend Sir, when placed on the Fortunate One’s body have lost their gleam!” “Just so, Ānanda, on two occasions, Ānanda,
dn16:4.37.6: the Realised One’s skin-colour becomes exceedingly pure and clean.
dn16:4.38.2: That night, Ānanda, the Realised One perfectly awakens to the unsurpassed and Perfect Awakening, and that night the Realised One is Finally Emancipated in the Emancipation-element which has no basis for attachment remaining.
dn16:4.38.3: On these two occasions the Realised One’s skin-colour is exceedingly pure and clean.
dn16:4.38.4: Today, Ānanda, during the last watch of the night, near to Kusinārā, in the Mallas’ Sal Wood at Upavattana, between a pair of Sal trees will be the Realised One’s Final Emancipation.
dn16:4.38.5: “Come Ānanda let us approach River Kakutthā.”
dn16:4.38.6: “Very well, reverend Sir,” venerable Ānanda replied to the Fortunate One.
