dn16:4.39.1: Then the Fortunate One with a great Community of monks went to the river Kakutthā, and after going, and entering into the river Kakutthā, bathing, and drinking, and coming back out, he approached the mango wood,
dn16:4.39.2: and after approaching, he addressed venerable Cundaka, (saying):
dn16:4.39.3: “Come now, Cundaka, prepare the outer robe folded in four for me, I am weary, Cundaka, and will lie down.”
dn16:4.40.1: “Very well, reverend Sir”, said venerable Cundaka, and after replying to the Fortunate One, he prepared the outer robe folded in four.
dn16:4.40.2: Then the Fortunate One, lay down on his right side in the lion’s posture, after placing one foot on the top of the other, mindfully, with full awareness, having applied his mind to the thought of rising.
dn16:4.40.3: And venerable Cundaka sat down right there in front of the Fortunate One.
dn16:4.41.1: “The Awakened One, having gone to the little river Kakutthā,
dn16:4.41.2: Which had water that was transparent, pleasant, and clear,
dn16:4.41.3: The Teacher, very weary, entered (the river),
dn16:4.41.4: the Realised One, who is unmatched here in the world.
dn16:4.41.5: After washing and drinking, the Teacher came out,
dn16:4.41.6: And in the middle of the Community of monks, at the front,
dn16:4.41.7: The Teacher, the Fortunate One, having taught the Teaching here,
dn16:4.41.8: The Great Sage went to the mango wood.
dn16:4.41.9: He addressed the monk called Cundaka, (saying):
dn16:4.41.10: “Spread out (the robe) folded in four for me to lie down on,”
dn16:4.41.11: Cunda, urged by the One with Developed Mind,
dn16:4.41.12: Very quickly spread (the robe) folded in four.
dn16:4.41.13: The Teacher, very weary, lay down,
dn16:4.41.14: With Cunda sat right there at the front.”
dn16:4.42.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:4.42.2: “It may be, Ānanda, that someone might cause remorse for the smith Cunda, (saying):
dn16:4.42.3: ‘There is no gain for you, friend Cunda, it is a poor gain for you, in that the Realised One, after eating his last almsfood from you, attained Final Emancipation.’
dn16:4.42.4: If there is remorse for Cunda the Smith, Ānanda, drive it out in this way, (saying):
dn16:4.42.5: ‘There is a gain for you, friend Cunda, it is a good gain for you,
dn16:4.42.6: in that the Realised One, after eating his last almsfood from you, attained Final Emancipation.
dn16:4.42.7: I heard this face to face with the Fortunate One, friend Cunda, I learned it face to face:
dn16:4.42.8: ‘There are these two almsfoods which have the very same excellent fruit, have the very same excellent result, that is a greater fruit, a greater result than other almsfood.
dn16:4.42.10: That almsfood which, after eating, the Realised One awakens to the unsurpassed and Perfect Awakening; and that almsfood which, after eating, the Realised One attains Final Emancipation in the Emancipation-element which has no basis for attachment remaining.
dn16:4.42.11: These are the two almsfoods which have the same fruit, have the same result, that is an exceedingly greater fruit, a greater result than other almsfood.
dn16:4.42.12: Friend Cunda the Smith has accumulated a (good) deed that is conducive to long life, friend Cunda the Smith has accumulated a (good) deed that is conducive to beauty, friend Cunda the Smith has accumulated a (good) deed that is conducive to happiness, friend Cunda the Smith has accumulated a (good) deed that is conducive to fame, friend Cunda the Smith has accumulated a (good) deed that is conducive to heaven, * friend Cunda the Smith has accumulated a (good) deed that is conducive to sovereignty.’
dn16:4.42.13: (If) there is remorse for Cunda the Smith, Ānanda, it should be driven out in this way!”
dn16:4.43.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
dn16:4.43.2: “For the one who gives merit is increased,
dn16:4.43.3: From restraint hatred is not accumulated.
dn16:4.43.4: The skilful one gives up what is bad,
dn16:4.43.5: Through the destruction of passion, hatred, and delusion, he is emancipated.”
dn16:5.1.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:5.1.2: * “Come Ānanda, let us approach the further shore of the Golden river, to Kusinārā, and to the Mallas’ Sal Wood at Upavattana.”
dn16:5.1.3: “Very well, reverend Sir,” venerable Ānanda replied to the Fortunate One.
dn16:5.1.4: Then the Fortunate One together with a great Community of monks * went to the further shore of the Golden river, to Kusinārā, and the Mallas’ Sal Wood at Upavattana, and after going he addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:5.1.5: * “Come, Ānanda, prepare a couch with the head facing north between the Twin Sal Trees for me, I am weary, Ānanda, and will lie down.”
dn16:5.1.6: “Very well, reverend Sir,” said venerable Ānanda, and after replying to the Fortunate One, he prepared a couch with the head facing north between the Twin Sal Trees.
dn16:5.1.7: Then the Fortunate One, lay down on his right side in the lion’s posture, after placing one foot on the top of the other, mindfully, with full awareness.
dn16:5.2.1: Now at that time the Twin Sal Trees were full of flowering blossoms, outside of flowering time,
dn16:5.2.2: and they were sprinkling down on the Realised One’s body, showering down, pouring down on the Realised One in worship.
dn16:5.2.3: Also the Divine Coral Tree flowers were falling from the sky, and they were sprinkling down on the Realised One’s body, showering down, pouring down on the Realised One in worship.
dn16:5.2.4: Also Divine sandalwood powder was falling from the sky, and was sprinkling down on the Realised One’s body, showering down, pouring down on the Realised One in worship.
dn16:5.2.5: Also Divine music played in the sky in worship of the Realised One.
dn16:5.2.6: Also Divine songs played in the sky in worship of the Realised One.
dn16:5.3.1: Then the Fortunate One said this to venerable Ānanda:
dn16:5.3.2: “The Twin Sal Trees are full of flowering blossoms, outside of flowering time,
dn16:5.3.3: and they are sprinkling down on the Realised One’s body, showering down, pouring down on the Realised One in worship.
dn16:5.3.4: Also the Divine Coral Tree flowers are falling from the sky, and they are sprinkling down on the Realised One’s body, showering down, pouring down on the Realised One in worship.
dn16:5.3.5: Also Divine sandalwood powder is falling from the sky, and is sprinkling down on the Realised One’s body, showering down, pouring down on the Realised One in worship.
dn16:5.3.6: Also Divine music plays in the sky in worship of the Realised One.
dn16:5.3.7: Also Divine songs play in the sky in worship of the Realised One.
dn16:5.3.8: But it is not in this way, Ānanda, that the Realised One is honoured, respected, revered, worshipped, or esteemed.
dn16:5.3.9: But that monk, nun, layman, or laywoman, Ānanda, who lives practising the Teaching in accordance with the Teaching, correct in their practice, living in conformity with the Teaching, he honours, respects, reveres, worships, and esteems the Realised One with the highest worship.
dn16:5.3.10: Therefore, Ānanda, thinking: ‘Let us live practising the Teaching in accordance with the Teaching, correct in our practice,
dn16:5.3.11: living in conformity with the Teaching,’ this is how you are to train, Ānanda.”
dn16:5.4.1: Now at that time venerable Upavāṇa was standing in front of the Fortunate One, fanning the Fortunate One.
dn16:5.4.2: Then the Fortunate One dismissed venerable Upavāṇa, (saying):
dn16:5.4.3: “Depart, monk, do not stand in front of me.”
dn16:5.4.5: “This venerable Upavāṇa has been the Fortunate One’s attendant for a long time, living near to him, within proximity.
dn16:5.4.6: Then at the last moment the Fortunate One dismisses venerable Upavāṇa, (saying):
dn16:5.4.7: ‘Depart, monk, do not stand in front of me.’
dn16:5.4.8: What was the reason, what was the cause, for the Fortunate One dismissing venerable Upavāṇa, (saying):
dn16:5.4.9: ‘Depart, monk, do not stand in front of me.’?”
dn16:5.5.1: Then venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:5.5.2: “This venerable Upavāṇa has been the Fortunate One’s attendant for a long time, living near to him, within proximity.
dn16:5.5.3: Then at the last moment the Fortunate One dismisses venerable Upavāṇa, (saying):
dn16:5.5.4: ‘Depart, monk, do not stand in front of me.’
dn16:5.5.5: What is the reason, reverend Sir, what is the cause, for the Fortunate One dismissing venerable Upavāṇa, (saying):
dn16:5.5.6: ‘Depart, monk, do not stand in front of me’?”
dn16:5.5.7: “Almost all of the Divinities, Ānanda, from the ten world-elements have assembled to see the Realised One,
dn16:5.5.8: everywhere around Kusinārā and the Mallas’ Sal Wood at Upavattana for as far as twelve leagues there is no place, even so much as a tip of a pricking hair, unpervaded by powerful Divinities,
dn16:5.5.9: and the Divinities, Ānanda, are complaining,
dn16:5.5.10: (saying): ‘We have come from afar to see the Realised One,
dn16:5.5.11: only occasionally, infrequently, do Realised Ones, Worthy Ones, Perfect Sambuddhas arise in the world,
dn16:5.5.12: and today during the last watch of the night will be the Realised One’s Final Emancipation,
dn16:5.5.13: and this powerful monk is stood in front concealing the Realised One, and we are not able to see the Realised One at the last moment.’”
dn16:5.6.1: “But what beings and Divinities is the Fortunate One thinking of?”
dn16:5.6.2: “There are, Ānanda, Divinities in the sky, perceiving the Earth, who, having dishevelled hair, are weeping, throwing up their arms, falling down (as though) cut down, rolling backwards and forwards as though with their feet cut off, they are crying:
dn16:5.6.3: ‘Too quickly the Fortunate One will attain Final Emancipation, too quickly the Happy One will attain Final Emancipation, too quickly the Visionary in the world will disappear!’
dn16:5.6.4: There are, Ānanda, Divinities on the Earth, perceiving the Earth, who, having dishevelled hair, are weeping, throwing up their arms, falling down (as though) cut down, rolling backwards and forwards as though with their feet cut off, they are crying:
dn16:5.6.5: ‘Too quickly the Fortunate One will attain Final Emancipation, too quickly the Happy One will attain Final Emancipation, too quickly the Visionary in the world will disappear!’”
dn16:5.6.6: But those Divinities who have cut off passion, mindfully, with full awareness, they endure, (thinking):
dn16:5.6.7: ‘Impermanent are (all) processes, how can it be otherwise?’”
dn16:5.7.1: “Formerly, reverend Sir, the monks, having dwelt for the Rains Retreat used to come to see the Realised One,
dn16:5.7.2: and we would receive those meditating monks for assembling and seeing (the Realised One).
dn16:5.7.3: But after the Fortunate One has passed way, reverend Sir, we will not receive those meditating monks for assembling and seeing (the Realised One).”
dn16:5.8.1: “There are these four places that can be seen, that produce enthusiasm, Ānanda, for a faithful man of good family.
dn16:5.8.3: (Thinking): ‘Here the Realised One was born’, Ānanda, (that) is a place to be seen that produces enthusiasm for a faithful man of good family.
dn16:5.8.4: (Thinking): ‘Here the Realised One awoke to the unsurpassed and Perfect Awakening’, Ānanda, (that) is a place to be seen that produces enthusiasm for a faithful man of good family.
dn16:5.8.5: (Thinking): ‘Here the Realised One set rolling the Wheel of the Teaching’, Ānanda, (that) is a place to be seen that produces enthusiasm for a faithful man of good family.
dn16:5.8.6: (Thinking): ‘Here the Realised One was completely Emancipated in the Emancipation-element which has no basis for attachment remaining’, Ānanda, (that) is a place to be seen that produces enthusiasm for a faithful man of good family.
dn16:5.8.7: * These are the four places, Ānanda, that are to be seen that produce enthusiasm for a faithful man of good family.
dn16:5.8.8: Faithful monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen will come, (thinking):
dn16:5.8.9: ‘Here the Realised One was born’, ‘Here the Realised One awoke to the unsurpassed and Perfect Awakening’, ‘Here the Realised One set rolling the Wheel of the Teaching’, ‘Here the Realised One was Finally Emancipated in the Emancipation-element which has no basis for attachment remaining’,
dn16:5.8.10: and whoever, Ānanda, will die while on pilgrimage to the Shrines with a confident mind they will all, at the break-up of the body, after death, re-arise in a happy destiny, in a heavenly world.”
dn16:5.9.1: “How, reverend Sir, are we to act in regard to women?”
dn16:5.9.2: “(As though they were) not seen, Ānanda.”
dn16:5.9.3: “(But) when seeing them, reverend Sir, how are we to act?”
dn16:5.9.5: “(But) when conversing, reverend Sir, how are we to act?”
dn16:5.10.1: “How should we act, reverend Sir, in regard to the Realised One’s body?”
dn16:5.10.2: “Do not worry, Ānanda, about how you are to worshipfully (dispose of) the Realised One’s body.
dn16:5.10.3: * Come, Ānanda, live striving for the highest good, being devoted to the highest good, being heedful of the highest good, ardent, and resolute.
dn16:5.10.4: There are, Ānanda, wise Nobles, wise brahmins, wise householders who have faith in the Realised One. They will worshipfully (dispose of) the Realised One’s body.”
dn16:5.11.1: “How should we act, reverend Sir, in regard to the Realised One’s body?”
dn16:5.11.2: “As you act in regard to the Universal Monarch’s body, so you should act in regard to the Realised One’s body.”
dn16:5.11.3: “But how do they act, reverend Sir, in regard to the Universal Monarch’s body?”
dn16:5.11.4: “They wrap the Universal Monarch’s body, Ānanda, with clean cloth, and after wrapping with clean cloth, they wrap with carded cotton, and after wrapping with carded cotton, they wrap with clean cloth,
dn16:5.11.5: by this means after wrapping the Universal Monarch’s body with five-hundred pairs (of cloth and cotton), enclosing it in an oil tub made of iron, and enclosing it in another iron tub, and putting it on a scented funeral pyre, they burn the Universal Monarch’s body,
dn16:5.11.6: and they build a Shrine for the Universal Monarch at the crossroads.
dn16:5.11.7: So they act in regard to a Universal Monarch’s body,
dn16:5.11.8: and as they act in regard to a Universal Monarch’s body so should they act in regard to a Realised One’s body,
dn16:5.11.9: and a Shrine should be made for the Realised One at the crossroads.
dn16:5.11.10: Whoever there prepares flowers, incense, or powder, or worships or establishes confidence in his mind, that will be for their benefit and happiness for a long time.
dn16:5.12.1: These four (persons), Ānanda, are worthy of a Shrine.
dn16:5.12.3: A Realised One, a Worthy One, a Perfect Sambuddha is worthy of a Shrine, an Individual Sambuddha is worthy of a Shrine, a Realised One’s disciple is worthy of a Shrine, a Universal Monarch is worthy of a Shrine.
dn16:5.12.4: And for what reason or cause is a Realised One, a Worthy One, a Perfect Sambuddha worthy of a Shrine?
dn16:5.12.5: (Thinking): ‘This is the Shrine of a Realised One, a Worthy One, a Perfect Sambuddha’, Ānanda, many people purify their mind,
dn16:5.12.6: and after purifying their mind, at the break-up of the body, after death, they arise in a happy destiny, in a Heavenly world.
dn16:5.12.7: This is the reason or cause, Ānanda, why a Realised One, a Worthy One, a Perfect Sambuddha is worthy of a Shrine.
dn16:5.12.8: And for what reason or cause is an Individual Sambuddha worthy of a Shrine?
dn16:5.12.9: (Thinking): ‘This is the Shrine of a Fortunate One, an Individual Sambuddha’, Ānanda, many people purify their mind,
dn16:5.12.10: and after purifying their mind, at the break-up of the body, after death, they arise in a happy destiny, in a Heavenly world.
dn16:5.12.11: This is the reason or cause, Ānanda, why an Individual Sambuddha is worthy of a Shrine.
dn16:5.12.12: And for what reason or cause is a Realised One’s disciple worthy of a Shrine?
dn16:5.12.13: (Thinking): ‘This is the Shrine of a disciple of a Fortunate One, a Worthy One, a Perfect Sambuddha’, Ānanda, many people purify their mind,
dn16:5.12.14: and after purifying their mind, at the break-up of the body, after death, they arise in a happy destiny, in a Heavenly world.
dn16:5.12.15: This is the reason or cause, Ānanda, why a Realised One’s disciple is worthy of a Shrine.
dn16:5.12.16: And for what reason or cause is a Universal Monarch worthy of a Shrine?
dn16:5.12.17: (Thinking): ‘This is the Shrine of a Righteous Monarch, a Righteous King’, Ānanda, many people purify their mind,
dn16:5.12.18: and after purifying their mind, at the break-up of the body, after death, they arise in a happy destiny, in a Heavenly world.
dn16:5.12.19: This is the reason or cause, Ānanda, why a Universal Monarch is worthy of a Shrine.
dn16:5.12.20: These, Ānanda, are the four (persons) worthy of a Shrine.”
dn16:5.13.1: Then venerable Ānanda, after entering the living place, and leaning against the door-lintel, stood there crying:
dn16:5.13.2: “The Teacher will attain Final Emancipation while I am still a Trainee with much to do, he who has compassion for me!”
dn16:5.13.3: Then the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
dn16:5.13.5: “This venerable Ānanda, reverend Sir, after entering the living place, and leaning against the door-lintel, stands there crying:
dn16:5.13.6: ‘The Teacher will attain Final Emancipation while I am still a Trainee with much to do, he who has compassion for me!’”
dn16:5.13.7: Then the Fortunate One addressed a certain monk, (saying):
dn16:5.13.8: “Go, monk, and in my name address Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:5.13.9: ‘The Teacher, friend Ānanda, is calling you.’”
dn16:5.13.10: “Very well, reverend Sir, and after replying to the Fortunate One, he approached venerable Ānanda, and after approaching he said this to venerable Ānanda:
dn16:5.13.11: “The Teacher, friend Ānanda, is calling you.”
dn16:5.14.1: “Very well, friend,” said venerable Ānanda, and after replying to that monk, he approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side the Fortunate One said this to venerable Ānanda:
dn16:5.14.2: “Enough, Ānanda, don't grieve, don't lament, were you not warned by me when I declared:
dn16:5.14.3: ‘There is alteration in, separation from, and changeability in all that is dear and appealing.’ How can it be otherwise, Ānanda, for that which is obtained,
dn16:5.14.4: born, become, conditioned, subject to dissolution? It is not possible (to say) this: ‘The Realised One’s body should not dissolve’.
dn16:5.14.5: For a long time, Ānanda, you dwelt near to the Realised One with beneficial, pleasant, trustworthy, and limitlessly friendly bodily actions, with beneficial, pleasant, trustworthy, and limitlessly friendly speech actions, with beneficial, pleasant, trustworthy, and limitlessly friendly mental actions,
dn16:5.14.6: you have done meritorious deeds, Ānanda, you should devote yourself to quickly striving to be one who is pollutant-free!”
dn16:5.15.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
dn16:5.15.2: “Whoever were Worthy Ones, Perfect Sambuddhas in the past, monks, for those Fortunate Ones also there were such superior attendants, just as Ānanda is for me;
dn16:5.15.3: whoever will be Worthy Ones, Perfect Sambuddhas in the future, monks, for those Fortunate Ones also there will be such superior attendants, just as Ānanda is for me.
dn16:5.15.5: Ānanda is intelligent, monks, he knows:
dn16:5.15.6: ‘This is the time for monks to approach and see the Realised One, this is the time for nuns, this is the time for laymen, this is the time for laywomen, this is the time for kings, for kings’ ministers, for outside teachers, for the disciples of outside teachers.’
dn16:5.16.1: There are four wonderful and marvellous things, monks, about Ānanda.
dn16:5.16.3: If, monks, a group of monks approach to see Ānanda their minds are uplifted through seeing (him),
dn16:5.16.4: and if Ānanda speaks words of welcome, their minds are uplifted with the speech,
dn16:5.16.5: but that group of monks are dissatisfied if at that time Ānanda remains silent.
dn16:5.16.6: If, monks, a group of nuns approach to see Ānanda their minds are uplifted through seeing (him),
dn16:5.16.7: and if Ānanda speaks words of welcome, their minds are uplifted with the speech,
dn16:5.16.8: but that group of nuns are dissatisfied if at that time Ānanda remains silent.
dn16:5.16.9: If, monks, a group of laymen approach to see Ānanda their minds are uplifted through seeing (him),
dn16:5.16.10: and if Ānanda speaks words of welcome, their minds are uplifted with the speech,
dn16:5.16.11: but that group of laymen are dissatisfied if at that time Ānanda remains silent.
dn16:5.16.12: If, monks, a group of laywomen approach to see Ānanda their minds are uplifted through seeing (him),
dn16:5.16.13: and if Ānanda speaks words of welcome, their minds are uplifted with the speech,
dn16:5.16.14: but that group of laywomen are dissatisfied if at that time Ānanda remains silent.
dn16:5.16.15: These are the four wonderful and marvellous things about Ānanda.
dn16:5.16.16: There are four wonderful and marvellous things, monks, about the Universal Monarch.
dn16:5.16.18: If, monks, a group of nobles approach to see the Universal Monarch their minds are uplifted through seeing (him),
dn16:5.16.19: and if the Universal Monarch speaks, their minds are uplifted with the speech,
dn16:5.16.20: but that group of nobles are dissatisfied if then the Universal Monarch remains silent.
dn16:5.16.21: If, monks, a group of brahmins approach to see the Universal Monarch their minds are uplifted through seeing (him), and if the Universal Monarch speaks, their minds are uplifted with the speech, but that group of brahmins are dissatisfied if then the Universal Monarch remains silent.
dn16:5.16.22: If, monks, a group of householders approach to see the Universal Monarch
dn16:5.16.23: their minds are uplifted through seeing (him), and if the Universal Monarch speaks, their minds are uplifted with the speech, but that group of householders are dissatisfied if then the Universal Monarch remains silent. If, monks, a group of ascetics approach to see the Universal Monarch their minds are uplifted through seeing (him),
dn16:5.16.24: and if the Universal Monarch speaks, their minds are uplifted with the speech,
dn16:5.16.25: but that group of ascetics are dissatisfied if then the Universal Monarch remains silent.
dn16:5.16.26: In the same way there are four wonderful and marvellous things, monks, about Ānanda.
dn16:5.16.27: If, monks, a group of monks approach to see Ānanda their minds are uplifted through seeing (him),
dn16:5.16.28: and if Ānanda speaks words of welcome, their minds are uplifted with the speech,
dn16:5.16.29: but that group of monks are dissatisfied
dn16:5.16.30: if at that time Ānanda remains silent.
dn16:5.16.31: If, monks, a group of nuns approach to see Ānanda their minds are uplifted through seeing (him), and if Ānanda speaks words of welcome, their minds are uplifted with the speech, but that group of nuns are dissatisfied if at that time Ānanda remains silent.
dn16:5.16.32: If, monks, a group of laymen approach to see Ānanda
dn16:5.16.33: their minds are uplifted through seeing (him),
dn16:5.16.34: and if Ānanda speaks words of welcome, their minds are uplifted with the speech,
dn16:5.16.35: but that group of laymen are dissatisfied if at that time Ānanda remains silent. If, monks, a group of laywomen approach to see Ānanda their minds are uplifted through seeing (him), and if Ānanda speaks words of welcome, their minds are uplifted with the speech,
dn16:5.16.36: but that group of laywomen are dissatisfied if at that time Ānanda remains silent.
dn16:5.16.37: There are the four wonderful and marvellous things, monks, about Ānanda.”
dn16:5.17.1: After this was said, venerable Ānanda addressed the Fortunate One, (saying):
dn16:5.17.2: * “Reverend Sir, may the Fortunate One not attain Final Emancipation in this small town, this barren town, this branch town.
dn16:5.17.3: There are, reverend Sir, other great towns, such as:
dn16:5.17.4: Campā, Rājagaha, Sāvatthī, Sāketa, Kosambī, Bārāṇasī -
dn16:5.17.5: let the Fortunate One attain Final Emancipation there.
dn16:5.17.6: There are many wealthy Nobles there, wealthy brahmins, wealthy householders,
dn16:5.17.7: who are devoted to the Realised One, and will worshipfully (dispose of) the Realised One’s body.”
dn16:5.17.8: “Do not say that, Ānanda, do not say that, Ānanda:
dn16:5.17.9: ‘(This) small town, this barren town, this branch town’.
dn16:5.18.1: Formerly, Ānanda, there was a King by the name of Mahāsudassana, a Righteous Monarch, a Righteous King, who was victorious over the four quarters, one who had established a stable country, endowed with the seven jewels.
dn16:5.18.2: This Kusinārā, was then named Kusāvatī, and was King Mahāsudassana’s capital city.
dn16:5.18.3: Stretching for twelve leagues from East to West, and seven leagues from North to South,
dn16:5.18.4: the capital city Kusāvatī was prosperous, Ānanda, successful, populous, full of people, with much food,
dn16:5.18.5: just as, Ānanda, the capital city of the Divinities named Āḷakamandā is prosperous, successful, populous, full of people, with much food,
dn16:5.18.6: so the capital city Kusāvatī was prosperous, Ānanda, successful, populous, full of people, with much food.
dn16:5.18.7: The capital city Kusāvatī was never separated from the ten sounds, by day or by night, that is to say: the sound of elephants, the sound of horses, the sound of chariots, the sound of drums,
dn16:5.18.8: the sound of tabours, the sound of lutes, the sound of songs, the sound of cymbals, the sound of hand bells, (and with) ‘eat, drink, chew!’ as the tenth sound.
dn16:5.19.1: “Go, Ānanda, and after entering into Kusinārā, announce to the Mallas:
dn16:5.19.2: ‘Today, Vāseṭṭhas, in the last watch of the night, will be the Realised One’s attainment of Final Emancipation,
dn16:5.19.3: come along, Vāseṭṭhas, come along, Vāseṭṭhas,
dn16:5.19.5: “In the area of our village, was the Realised One’s attainment of Final Emancipation, and we did not, in the last watch of the night, get to see the Realised One”’.”
dn16:5.19.6: “Very well, reverend Sir,” said venerable Ānanda, and after replying to the Fortunate One, dressing, and taking his robes and bowl, he entered Kusinārā with a companion.
dn16:5.20.1: Now at that time the Mallas from Kusinārā were assembled in the Council Hall having some business or other.
dn16:5.20.2: Then venerable Ānanda went to where the Mallas from Kusinārā were assembled in the Council Hall, and after approaching he said this to the Mallas:
dn16:5.20.3: “Today, Vāseṭṭhas, in the last watch of the night, will be the Realised One’s attainment of Final Emancipation,
dn16:5.20.4: come along, Vāseṭṭhas, come along, Vāseṭṭhas,
dn16:5.20.6: ‘In the area of our village, was the Realised One’s attainment of Final Emancipation, and we did not, in the last watch of the night, get to see the Realised One.’”
dn16:5.21.1: After hearing this from venerable Ānanda, the Mallas, the sons of the Mallas, the daughters-in-law of the Mallas, and the wives of the Mallas became miserable, depressed, with their minds given over to suffering. Some, having dishevelled hair, were weeping, throwing up their arms, falling down (as though) cut down, rolling backwards and forwards as though with their feet cut off, they were crying:
dn16:5.21.2: “Too quickly the Fortunate One will attain Final Emancipation, too quickly the Happy One will attain Final Emancipation, too quickly the Visionary in the world will disappear!”
dn16:5.21.3: Then the Mallas, the sons of the Mallas, the daughters-in-law of the Mallas, and the wives of the Mallas, miserable, depressed, with their minds given over to suffering, approached the Mallas’ Sal Wood at Upavattana, and approached venerable Ānanda.
dn16:5.22.1: Then this occurred to venerable Ānanda:
dn16:5.22.2: “If I make the Mallas of Kusinārā worship the Fortunate One one by one before the Fortunate One has been worshipped by the Mallas of Kusinārā the night will end.
dn16:5.22.3: Now what if I, having segregated the Mallas family by family, made them worship the Fortunate One, (saying):
dn16:5.22.4: ‘A Malla named so and so, together with his children, wife, dependents, and councillors worships the Fortunate One’s feet with his head'?”
dn16:5.22.5: Then venerable Ānanda having segregated the Mallas family by family, made them worship the Fortunate One, (saying):
dn16:5.22.6: “A Malla named so and so, together with his children, wife, dependents, and councillors worships the Fortunate One’s feet with his head.”
dn16:5.22.7: Then venerable Ānanda, in this way, during the first watch of the night, made the Mallas of Kusinārā worship the Fortunate One.
dn16:5.23.1: Now at that time a wanderer named Subhadda had arrived at Kusinārā.
dn16:5.23.3: “Today, it seems, in the last watch of the night, will be the ascetic Gotama’s attainment of Final Emancipation.”
dn16:5.23.4: Then this occurred to the wanderer Subhadda:
dn16:5.23.5: “I have heard this from old, elderly wanderers, who are teachers and teachers’ teachers, when they said:
dn16:5.23.6: ‘Only occasionally, rarely, do Realised Ones, Worthy Ones, Perfect Sambuddhas arise in the world.’
dn16:5.23.7: Today, in the last watch of the night, will be the ascetic Gotama’s attainment of Final Emancipation.
dn16:5.23.8: There is a doubt that has arisen for me,
dn16:5.23.9: and I have confidence in the ascetic Gotama thus: ‘The ascetic Gotama is able to teach the Teaching in such a way that I will be able to abandon that doubt.’”
dn16:5.24.1: Then the wanderer Subhadda approached the Mallas’ Sal Wood at Upavattana, and approached venerable Ānanda, and after approaching he said to venerable Ānanda:
dn16:5.24.2: “I have heard this from old, elderly wanderers, dear Ānanda, who are teachers and teachers’ teachers, when they said:
dn16:5.24.3: ‘Only occasionally, rarely, do Realised Ones, Worthy Ones, Perfect Sambuddhas arise in the world.’
dn16:5.24.4: Today, in the last watch of the night, will be the ascetic Gotama’s attainment of Final Emancipation.
dn16:5.24.5: There is a doubt that has arisen for me,
dn16:5.24.6: and I have confidence in the ascetic Gotama thus: ‘The ascetic Gotama is able to teach the Teaching in such a way that I will be able to abandon that doubt’.
dn16:5.24.7: It would be well, dear Ānanda, if I was allowed to see the ascetic Gotama.”
dn16:5.24.8: After this was said, venerable Ānanda said this to the wanderer Subhadda:
dn16:5.24.9: “Enough, friend Subhadda, do not trouble the Realised One, the Fortunate One is exhausted.”
dn16:5.24.10: For a second time the wanderer Subhadda said this to venerable Ānanda: “I have heard this from old, elderly wanderers, dear Ānanda, who are teachers and teachers’ teachers, when they said: ‘Only occasionally, rarely, do Realised Ones, Worthy Ones, Perfect Sambuddhas arise in the world.’ Today, in the last watch of the night, will be the Realised One’s attainment of Final Emancipation. There is a doubt that has arisen for me, and I have confidence in the ascetic Gotama thus: ‘The ascetic Gotama is able to teach the Teaching in such a way that I will be able to abandon that doubt’. It would be well, dear Ānanda, if I was allowed to see the ascetic Gotama. For a second time venerable Ānanda said this to the wanderer Subhadda: “Enough, friend Subhadda, do not trouble the Realised One, the Fortunate One is exhausted.”
dn16:5.24.11: For a third time the wanderer Subhadda said this to venerable Ānanda:
dn16:5.24.12: “I have heard this from old, elderly wanderers, dear Ānanda, who are teachers and teachers’ teachers, when they said:
dn16:5.24.13: ‘Only occasionally, rarely, do Realised Ones, Worthy Ones, Perfect Sambuddhas arise in the world.’
dn16:5.24.14: Today, in the last watch of the night, will be the ascetic Gotama’s attainment of Final Emancipation.
dn16:5.24.15: There is a doubt that has arisen for me,
dn16:5.24.16: and I have confidence in the ascetic Gotama thus: ‘The ascetic Gotama is able to teach the Teaching in such a way that I will be able to abandon that doubt’.
dn16:5.24.17: It would be well, dear Ānanda, if I was allowed to see the ascetic Gotama.”
dn16:5.24.18: For a third time venerable Ānanda said this to the wanderer Subhadda:
dn16:5.24.19: “Enough, friend Subhadda, do not trouble the Realised One, the Fortunate One is exhausted.”
dn16:5.25.1: The Fortunate One heard venerable Ānanda having this conversation with the wanderer Subhadda.
dn16:5.25.2: Then the Fortunate One said this to venerable Ānanda:
dn16:5.25.3: “Enough, Ānanda, do not obstruct Subhadda allow Subhadda to see the Realised One.
dn16:5.25.4: Whatever Subhadda will ask of me all of it he will ask of me seeking for deep knowledge, and not to trouble me.
dn16:5.25.5: Whatever question is put I will answer, and he will quickly understand it.”
dn16:5.25.6: Then venerable Ānanda said this to the wanderer Subhadda:
dn16:5.25.7: “Go, friend Subhadda, the Fortunate One has given you permission.”
dn16:5.26.1: Then the wanderer Subhadda approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching, he exchanged greetings with the Fortunate One, and after exchanging courteous talk and greetings, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side the wanderer Subhadda said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:5.26.2: “Those ascetics and brahmins, dear Gotama, who have a community, a group, who teach a group, well-known, famous, religious founders, agreed upon as good for the people,
dn16:5.26.3: such as: Pūraṇa Kassapa, Makkhali Gosāla, Ajita Kesakambala, Pakudha Kaccāyana, Sañjaya Belaṭṭhaputta, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta,
dn16:5.26.4: have they all understood, according to their own avowal? Have they all not understood? Or, have some understood? Or, have some not understood?”
dn16:5.26.6: ‘Have they all understood, according to their own avowal? Have they all not understood? Or, have some understood? Or, have some not understood?’
dn16:5.26.7: I will teach the Teaching to you, Subhadda,
dn16:5.26.8: listen to it, apply your mind well, and I will speak.”
dn16:5.26.9: “Very well, reverend Sir,” the wanderer Subhadda replied to the Fortunate One,
dn16:5.26.10: and the Fortunate One said this:
dn16:5.27.1: “Wherever, Subhadda, the Noble Eightfold Path is not found in a Teaching and Discipline there a (true) ascetic is not found, there a second (true) ascetic is not found, there a third (true) ascetic is not found, there a fourth (true) ascetic is not found.
dn16:5.27.2: But wherever, Subhadda, the Noble Eightfold Path is found in a Teaching and Discipline there a (true) ascetic is found, there a second (true) ascetic is found, there a third (true) ascetic is found, there a fourth (true) ascetic is found.
dn16:5.27.3: In this Teaching and Discipline, Subhadda, the Noble Eightfold Path is found, here a (true) ascetic is found, here a second (true) ascetic is found, here a third (true) ascetic is found, here a fourth (true) ascetic is found. Void are the outside doctrines of these other ascetics, Subhadda,
dn16:5.27.4: (but) if monks should live well, the world will not be void of Worthy Ones.
dn16:5.27.6: I went forth a seeker of what is good,
dn16:5.27.8: Wherefore I am (truly) gone forth, Subhadda.
dn16:5.27.9: Existing in the realm of the right Teaching
dn16:5.27.10: Outside of this there is no (true) ascetic,
dn16:5.27.11: a second (true) ascetic is not found,
dn16:5.27.12: a third (true) ascetic is not found,
dn16:5.27.13: a fourth (true) ascetic is not found.
dn16:5.27.14: Void are the outside doctrines of these other ascetics, Subhadda,
dn16:5.27.15: (but) if monks should live well, the world will not be void of Worthy Ones.”
dn16:5.28.1: After this was said, the wanderer Subhadda said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:5.28.3: Just as, reverend Sir, one might set upright what has been overturned, or open up what has been closed, or show a path to one who is lost, or bear an oil lamp in the darkness, so that one who has eyes can see forms, just so has the Teaching been made clear by the Fortunate One in more than one way.
dn16:5.28.4: I go to the Fortunate One for refuge, reverend Sir, and to the Teaching, and to the Community of monks.
dn16:5.28.5: May I receive the going-forth, reverend Sir, in the presence of the Fortunate One, may I receive the full ordination.”
dn16:5.29.1: “Those who were formerly of another sect who in this Teaching and Discipline desire the going-forth, who desire full ordination, live on probation for four months, and at the end of four months, the minds of the monks being satisfied, they give the going-forth and the full ordination into the monkhood.
dn16:5.29.2: But I understand there is a distinction between persons in this case.”
dn16:5.29.3: “If, reverend Sir, those who were formerly of another sect who in this Teaching and Discipline, desire the going-forth, who desire full ordination, live on probation for four months, and at the end of four months, the minds of the monks being satisfied, they give the going-forth and the full ordination into the monkhood, then I will live on probation for four years, and at the end of four years, the minds of the monks being satisfied, they can give the going-forth and the full ordination into the monkhood.”
dn16:5.29.4: Then the Fortunate One said this to venerable Ānanda:
dn16:5.29.5: “Then, Ānanda, give the going-forth to Subhadda.”
dn16:5.29.6: “Very well, reverend Sir,” venerable Ānanda replied to the Fortunate One.
dn16:5.30.1: Then the wanderer Subhadda said this to venerable Ānanda:
dn16:5.30.2: “There are certainly gains for you, friend Ānanda, it is certainly a good gain for you, friend Ānanda,
dn16:5.30.3: that here, face to face with the Teacher, you have been consecrated with an attendant’s consecration.”
dn16:5.30.4: The wanderer Subhadda received the going forth in the presence of the Fortunate One, received full ordination.
dn16:5.30.5: Then not long after ordination, venerable Subhadda, while dwelling solitary, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute, after no long time (attained) that good for which young gentlemen rightly go forth from the house to the houseless life, that unsurpassed conclusion to the spiritual life, and dwelt having known, experienced, and attained it himself in this very life.
dn16:5.30.6: Destroyed is (re)birth accomplished is the spiritual life done is what ought to be done there is no more of this mundane state - this he knew.
dn16:5.30.7: And venerable Subhadda became another of the Worthy Ones.
dn16:5.30.8: He was the last direct disciple of the Fortunate One.
dn16:6.1.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:6.1.2: “It may be, Ānanda, that some of you may think in this way:
dn16:6.1.3: ‘Past is the Teacher’s word, there is now no Teacher for us.’
dn16:6.1.4: But it should not be seen like that, Ānanda,
dn16:6.1.5: whatever Teaching and Discipline has been taught by me or laid down, Ānanda, that is your Teacher after my passing away.
dn16:6.2.1: At present, Ānanda, the monks address each other with the word ‘friend’, (but) after my passing away they are not to address (one another) thus.
dn16:6.2.2: * The elder monk, Ānanda, should address the younger monk by his name or by his clan (name) or by the word ‘friend’.
dn16:6.2.3: (But) the younger monk should address the elder monk as reverend Sir or venerable Sir.
dn16:6.3.1: Desiring (to do so), Ānanda, the Community after my passing away, can abolish the minor and subsidiary training rules.
dn16:6.4.1: The highest penalty, Ānanda, after my passing away, is to be handed out to the monk Channa.”
dn16:6.4.2: “But what is the highest penalty, reverend Sir?”
dn16:6.4.3: “The monk Channa, Ānanda, may say whatever he wishes
dn16:6.4.4: but he is not to be spoken to or advised or instructed by the monks.”
dn16:6.5.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
dn16:6.5.2: “It may be, monks, that for one of the monks there is doubt or confusion about the Buddha, or about the Teaching, or about the Community, or about the Path, or about the practice. Ask, monks, do not be regretful later (thinking):
dn16:6.5.3: ‘The Teacher was face to face with us and we didn't ask the Fortunate One directly about the training.’”
dn16:6.5.4: After this was said those monks were silent.
dn16:6.6.1: For a second time the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying): “It may be, monks, that for one of the monks there is doubt or confusion about the Buddha, or about the Teaching, or about the Community, or about the Path, or about the practice. Ask, monks, do not be regretful later (thinking): ‘The Teacher was face to face with us and we didn't ask the Fortunate One directly about the training.’” For a second time those monks were silent.
dn16:6.6.2: For a third time the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
dn16:6.6.3: “It may be, monks, that for one of the monks there is doubt or confusion about the Buddha, or about the Teaching, or about the Community, or about the Path, or about the practice. Ask, monks, do not be regretful later (thinking):
dn16:6.6.4: ‘The Teacher was face to face with us and we didn't ask the Fortunate One directly about the training.’”
dn16:6.6.5: For a third time those monks were silent.
dn16:6.6.6: Then the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
dn16:6.6.7: “It may be, monks, that out of respect for the Teacher you do not ask, then one friend, monks, can inform another friend (about his doubts).”
dn16:6.6.8: After this was said those monks were silent.
dn16:6.6.9: Then venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One:
dn16:6.6.10: “It is wonderful, reverend Sir, it is marvellous, reverend Sir, I am confident, reverend Sir, that in this Community of monks there is not one of the monks in this Community of monks who has doubt or confusion about the Buddha, or about the Teaching, or about the Community, or about the Path, or about the practice.”
dn16:6.6.11: “Out of confidence, Ānanda, you speak, but the Realised One, Ānanda, has knowledge that there is not one of the monks in this Community of monks who has doubt or confusion about the Buddha, or about the Teaching, or about the Community, or about the Path, or about the practice.
dn16:6.6.12: For amongst these five hundred monks, Ānanda, he who is the last monk, is a Stream-Enterer, no longer subject to falling (into the lower realms), and has a fixed destiny ending in Final Awakening.”
dn16:6.7.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
dn16:6.7.2: “Come now, monks, for I tell you (all) conditioned things are subject to decay,
dn16:6.7.4: These were the last words of the Realised One.
dn16:6.8.1: Then the Fortunate One attained the first absorption, and after emerging from the first absorption he attained the second absorption, and after emerging from the second absorption he attained the third absorption, and after emerging from the third absorption he attained the fourth absorption, and after emerging from the fourth absorption he attained the sphere of endless space, and after emerging from the sphere of endless space he attained the sphere of endless consciousness, and after emerging from the sphere of endless consciousness he attained the sphere of nothingness, and after emerging from the sphere of nothingness, he attained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and after emerging from the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he attained the cessation of perception and feeling.
dn16:6.8.2: Then venerable Ānanda said this to venerable Anuruddha:
dn16:6.8.3: “(Has) the Fortunate One, reverend Anuruddha, attained Final Emancipation?”
dn16:6.8.4: “The Fortunate One, reverend Ānanda, has not attained Final Emancipation, he has attained the cessation of perception and feeling.”
dn16:6.9.1: Then the Fortunate One, after emerging from the cessation of perception and feeling, attained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and after emerging from the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception he attained the sphere of nothingness, and after emerging from the sphere of nothingness he attained the sphere of endless consciousness, and after emerging from the sphere of endless consciousness he attained the sphere of endless space, and after emerging from the sphere of endless space he attained the fourth absorption, and after emerging from the fourth absorption he attained the third absorption, and after emerging from the third absorption he attained the second absorption, and after emerging from the second absorption he attained the first absorption, and after emerging from the first absorption he attained the second absorption, and after emerging from the second absorption he attained the third absorption, and after emerging from the third absorption he attained the fourth absorption, and after emerging from the fourth absorption, immediately the Fortunate One attained Final Emancipation.
dn16:6.10.1: When the Fortunate One attained Final Emancipation along with the Emancipation there was a great earthquake, and an awful, horrifying crash of the Divinities’ (thunder) drum.
dn16:6.10.2: When the Fortunate One attained Final Emancipation along with the Emancipation Brahmā Sahampati spoke this verse:
dn16:6.10.3: “All beings in the world will surely lay aside the body,
dn16:6.10.5: In the same way the Teacher, Such-like,
dn16:6.10.7: the Realised One, attained to (the ten) strengths, the Sambuddha, has attained Final Emancipation.”
dn16:6.10.8: When the Fortunate One attained Final Emancipation along with the Emancipation
dn16:6.10.9: Sakka, the Lord of the Divinities, spoke this verse:
dn16:6.10.11: arisen they have the nature to decay,
dn16:6.10.12: After arising they come to cessation,
dn16:6.10.13: the stilling of them is blissful.”
dn16:6.10.14: When the Fortunate One attained Final Emancipation along with the Emancipation venerable Anuruddha spoke these verses:
dn16:6.10.16: for that Such-like one of steady mind,
dn16:6.10.17: Freed from lust, the Sage who has died, has entered the peace (of Nibbāna).
dn16:6.10.21: Like a flame (when it goes out) so his mind was liberated in Nibbāna.”
dn16:6.10.23: When the Fortunate One attained Final Emancipation along with the Emancipation venerable Ānanda spoke this verse:
dn16:6.10.26: When the Sambuddha, endowed with all noble qualities, attained Emancipation.”
dn16:6.10.27: When the Fortunate One attained Final Emancipation those monks there who were not free from passion,
dn16:6.10.28: throwing up their arms, falling down (as though) cut down, rolling backwards and forwards as though with their feet cut off, were crying: ‘Too quickly the Fortunate One has attained Final Emancipation, too quickly the Happy One has attained Final Emancipation, too quickly the Visionary in the world has disappeared!’
dn16:6.10.29: But those monks who were free from passion, mindfully, with full awareness, endured, (thinking):
dn16:6.10.30: “Impermanent are (all) processes, how can it be otherwise?”
dn16:6.11.1: Then venerable Anuruddha said this to the monks:
dn16:6.11.2: “Enough, friends, do not grieve, do not lament,
dn16:6.11.3: were you not warned by the Fortunate One when he declared:
dn16:6.11.4: ‘There is alteration in, separation from, and changeability in all that is dear and appealing.’
dn16:6.11.5: How can it be otherwise, friends, for that which is obtained, born, become, in process, subject to dissolution? It is not possible (to say) this: ‘It should not dissolve’.
dn16:6.11.7: “But what beings and Divinities is the venerable Anuruddha thinking of?”
dn16:6.11.8: “There are, friend Ānanda, Divinities in the sky, perceiving the Earth, who, having dishevelled hair, are weeping, throwing up their arms, falling down (as though) cut down, rolling backwards and forwards as though with their feet cut off, crying:
dn16:6.11.9: ‘Too quickly the Fortunate One has attained Final Emancipation, too quickly the Happy One has attained Final Emancipation, too quickly the Visionary in the world has disappeared!’
dn16:6.11.10: There are, friend Ānanda, Divinities on the Earth, perceiving the Earth, who, having dishevelled hair, are weeping, throwing up their arms, falling down (as though) cut down, rolling backwards and forwards as though with their feet cut off, crying:
dn16:6.11.11: ‘Too quickly the Fortunate One has attained Final Emancipation, too quickly the Happy One has attained Final Emancipation, too quickly the Visionary in the world has disappeared!’
dn16:6.11.12: But those Divinities, who have cut off passion, they mindfully, with full awareness, endure, (thinking):
dn16:6.11.13: ‘Impermanent are (all) processes, how can it be otherwise?’”
dn16:6.11.14: Then venerable Anuruddha and venerable Ānanda spent the rest of the night in talk about the Teaching.
dn16:6.12.1: Then venerable Anuruddha addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
dn16:6.12.2: “Go, Ānanda, and after entering Kusinārā inform the Mallas of Kusinārā, (saying):
dn16:6.12.3: ‘The Fortunate One has attained Emancipation, Vāseṭṭhas, now is the time for whatever you are thinking.’”
dn16:6.12.5: “Very well, reverend Sir,” said venerable Ānanda, and after replying to venerable Anuruddha, dressing in the morning time, and taking his robes and bowl, he entered Kusinārā with a companion.
dn16:6.12.6: Now at that time the Mallas from Kusinārā were assembled in the Council Hall having some business (or other).
dn16:6.12.7: Then venerable Ānanda approached the Mallas from Kusinārā in the Council Hall, and after approaching he informed the Mallas of Kusinārā (saying):
dn16:6.12.8: “The Fortunate One has attained Emancipation, Vāseṭṭhas, now is the time for whatever you are thinking.”
dn16:6.12.10: After hearing this word from venerable Ānanda, the Mallas, the sons of the Mallas, the daughters-in-law of the Mallas, and the wives of the Mallas became miserable, depressed, with their minds given over to suffering. Some, having dishevelled hair, were weeping, throwing up their arms, falling down (as though) cut down, rolling backwards and forwards as though with their feet cut off, they were crying:
dn16:6.12.11: “Too quickly the Fortunate One has attained Final Emancipation, too quickly the Happy One has attained Final Emancipation, too quickly the Visionary in the world has disappeared!”
dn16:6.13.1: Then the Mallas from Kusinārā ordered (their) men, (saying):
dn16:6.13.2: * “Now, friends, gather together perfume and flowers, and all the musicians in Kusinārā.”
dn16:6.13.3: * Then the Mallas of Kusinārā, having taken perfumes and garlands, and all the musicians, and five-hundred pairs of clothes, approached the Mallas’ Sal Wood at Upavattana, and the Fortunate One’s body, after approaching the Fortunate One’s body, * through honouring, respecting, revering, and worshipping (the body), with dance, song, music, garlands, and perfumes, and making cloth canopies, and preparing circular pavillions, they made the day pass.
dn16:6.13.4: Then this occurred to the Mallas of Kusinārā:
dn16:6.13.5: “Today it is too late to burn the Fortunate One’s body, tomorrow we will burn the Fortunate One’s body.”
dn16:6.13.6: Then the Mallas of Kusinārā, * through honouring, respecting, revering, and worshipping the Fortunate One’s body, with dance, song, music, garlands, and perfumes, and making cloth canopies, and preparing circular pavillions, they made the second day pass, they made the third day pass, they made the fourth day pass, they made the fifth day pass, they made the sixth day pass.
dn16:6.14.1: Then on the seventh day this occurred to the Mallas of Kusinārā:
dn16:6.14.2: * “While honouring, respecting, revering, and worshipping the Fortunate One’s body, with dance, song, music, garlands, and perfumes, after taking it out of the city by the South, on the outside of the City to the South we will burn the Fortunate One’s body.”
dn16:6.14.3: Now at that time eight leaders of the Mallas, having washed their heads and put on clean clothes, (said):
dn16:6.14.4: “Let us lift the Fortunate One’s body,” but they were not able to lift (it).
dn16:6.14.5: Then the Mallas of Kusinārā said this to venerable Anuruddha:
dn16:6.14.6: “What is the reason, Anuruddha, what is the cause why eight leaders of the Mallas, having washed their heads and put on clean clothes, (and saying):
dn16:6.14.7: ‘Let us lift the Fortunate One’s body,’ are not able to lift (it)?”
dn16:6.14.8: “You Vāseṭṭhas have one intention, and the Divinities have another intention.”
dn16:6.15.1: “But what is the Divinities’ intention, reverend Sir?”
dn16:6.15.3: * ‘We, while honouring, respecting, revering, and worshipping the Fortunate One’s body, with dance, song, music, garlands, and perfumes, after taking it out of the City by the South, on the outside of the City to the South, will burn the Fortunate One’s body.’
dn16:6.15.5: ‘We, while honouring, respecting, revering, and worshipping the Fortunate One’s body, with the Divinities’ dance, song, music, garlands, and perfumes, after carrying it to the North of the City by the North, and re-entering the City by the North Gate, and carrying it to the middle of the City by the middle, and going out by the Eastern Gate, to the East of the City, at the Mallas’ Shrine called the Bonded Coronet, there let us burn the Fortunate One’s body.”
dn16:6.15.6: “Let us do according to the Divinities’ intention, reverend Sir.”
dn16:6.16.1: * Now at that time the whole of Kusinārā, including the dirty rubbish heaps, was covered knee-deep with (Divine) Coral Tree flowers.
dn16:6.16.2: Then the Divinities and the Mallas of Kusinārā * while honouring, respecting, revering, and worshipping the Fortunate One’s body with the Divinities’ and mens’ dance, song, music, garlands, and perfumes, after carrying it to the North of the City by the North, and re-entering the City by the North Gate, and carrying it to the middle of the City by the middle, and going out by the Eastern Gate, to the East of the City, at the Mallas’ Shrine called the Bonded Coronet there set down the Fortunate One’s body.
dn16:6.17.1: Then the Mallas of Kusinārā said this to venerable Ānanda:
dn16:6.17.2: “How do we act, reverend Ānanda, in regard to the Realised One’s body?”
dn16:6.17.3: “As you act, Vāseṭṭhas, in regard to the Universal Monarch’s body, so you should act in regard to the Realised One’s body.”
dn16:6.17.4: “But how do we act, reverend Ānanda, in regard to the Universal Monarch’s body?”
dn16:6.17.5: “They wrap the Universal Monarch’s body, Vāseṭṭhas, with clean cloth, and after wrapping with clean cloth, they wrap with carded cotton, and after wrapping with carded cotton, they wrap with clean cloth,
dn16:6.17.6: by this means after wrapping the Universal Monarch’s body with five-hundred pairs (of cloth and cotton), enclosing it in an oil tub made of iron, and enclosing it in another iron tub, and putting it on a scented funeral pyre, they burn the Universal Monarch’s body,
dn16:6.17.7: and they build a Shrine for the Universal Monarch at the crossroads.
dn16:6.17.8: So they act, Vāseṭṭhas, in regard to a Universal Monarch’s body.
dn16:6.17.9: Just as they act, Vāseṭṭhas, in regard to a Universal Monarch’s body, so should they act in regard to a Realised One’s body,
dn16:6.17.10: and a Shrine should be made for the Realised One at the crossroads.
dn16:6.17.11: Whoever there prepares flowers, incense, or powder, or worships or establishes confidence in his mind, that will be for their benefit and happiness for a long time.”
dn16:6.18.1: Then the Mallas of Kusinārā gave orders to (their) men, (saying):
dn16:6.18.2: “If it is so (then) wrap (the body) with the Mallas’ carded cloth, friends.”
dn16:6.18.3: Then the Mallas of Kusinārā wrapped the Fortunate One’s body with clean cloth, and after wrapping with clean cloth, they wrapped with carded cotton, and after wrapping with carded cotton, they wrapped with clean cloth,
dn16:6.18.4: and by this means, after wrapping the Fortunate One’s body with five-hundred pairs (of cloth and cotton), enclosing it in an oil tub made of iron, and enclosing it in another iron tub, and putting it on a scented funeral pyre, they put the Fortunate One’s body on the funeral pyre.
dn16:6.19.1: Now at that time venerable Mahākassapa was travelling along the highway from Pāvā to Kusinārā, together with a great Community of monks, around five-hundred monks.
dn16:6.19.2: Then venerable Mahākassapa, after descending from the path, sat down at the root of a certain tree.
dn16:6.19.3: Now at that time a certain Ājīvaka while holding a Mandārava flower from Kusinārā was travelling along the highway to Pāvā.
dn16:6.19.4: Venerable Mahākassapa saw that Ājīvaka approaching from afar, and after seeing (him), he said this to that Ājīvaka:
dn16:6.19.6: “Certainly, friend, I know. Today is seven days since the Final Emancipation of the ascetic Gotama,
dn16:6.19.7: therefore I am holding this Mandārava flower.”
dn16:6.19.8: Then those monks there who were not free from passion, some, throwing up their arms, were weeping, falling down (as though) cut down, rolling backwards and forwards as though with their feet cut off, they were crying:
dn16:6.19.9: ‘Too quickly the Fortunate One has attained Final Emancipation, too quickly the Happy One has attained Final Emancipation, too quickly the Visionary in the world has disappeared!’
dn16:6.19.10: But those monks who were free from passion, mindfully, with full awareness, endured, (thinking):
dn16:6.19.11: “Impermanent are (all) processes, how can it be otherwise?”
dn16:6.20.1: Now at that time one who had gone forth in old age, named Subhadda was sitting in that group.
dn16:6.20.2: Then Subhadda, who had gone forth in old age, said this to those monks:
dn16:6.20.3: “Enough, friends, do not grieve, do not lament, we are now freed from that troublesome Great Ascetic, (saying):
dn16:6.20.4: ‘This is allowable for you, this is not allowable for you.’
dn16:6.20.5: But now we will do whatever we wish, and we will not do whatever we do not wish.”
dn16:6.20.6: Then venerable Mahākassapa addressed the monks, (saying):
dn16:6.20.7: “Enough, friends, do not grieve, do not lament,
dn16:6.20.8: were you not warned by the Fortunate One, friends, when he declared this:
dn16:6.20.9: ‘There is alteration in, separation from, and changeability in all that is dear and appealing.’
dn16:6.20.10: How can it be otherwise, friends, for that which is obtained, born, become, in process, subject to dissolution? It is not possible (to say) this: ‘It should not dissolve’.
dn16:6.21.1: Now at that time four leaders of the Mallas, having washed their heads and put on clean clothes, (said):
dn16:6.21.2: “Let us burn the Fortunate One’s funeral pyre,” but they were not able to burn (it).
dn16:6.21.3: Then the Mallas of Kusinārā said this to venerable Anuruddha:
dn16:6.21.4: “What is the reason, venerable Anuruddha, what is the cause, why four leaders of the Mallas, having washed their heads and put on clean clothes, (and saying):
dn16:6.21.5: ‘Let us burn the Fortunate One’s funeral pyre,’ are not able to burn (it)?”
dn16:6.21.7: “But what is the Divinities’ intention, reverend Sir?”
dn16:6.21.9: ‘The venerable Mahākassapa is travelling along the highway from Pāvā to Kusinārā together with a great Community of monks, around five-hundred monks,
dn16:6.21.10: the Fortunate One’s funeral pyre will not burn while venerable Mahākassapa has not worshipped the Fortunate One’s feet with his head.’”
dn16:6.21.11: “Let us do according to the Divinities’ intention, reverend Sir.”
dn16:6.22.1: Then venerable Mahākassapa approached Kusinārā, and the Mallas’ Shrine called the Bonded Coronet, and the Fortunate One’s funeral pyre, and after approaching and arranging his robe on one shoulder, extending (his hands) in respectful salutation,
dn16:6.22.2: and circumambulating the funeral pyre three times, and uncovering the feet he worshipped the Fortunate One’s feet with his head. Also five-hundred monks, after arranging their robes on one shoulder, extending (their hands) in respectful salutation, and circumambulating the funeral pyre three times, worshipped the Fortunate One’s feet with their heads.
dn16:6.22.3: After (the Fortunate One’s feet) had been worshipped by venerable Mahākassapa and by five-hundred monks the funeral pyre caught fire by itself.
dn16:6.23.1: Now while the Fortunate One’s body was burning, of the outer skin, the inner skin, the flesh, the sinews, the synovial fluid,
dn16:6.23.2: neither charcoal was evident, nor was ash of the body left over.
dn16:6.23.3: Just as while ghee or oil is burning there is no charcoal and no ash evident,
dn16:6.23.4: so when the Fortunate One’s body was burning, of the outer skin, the inner skin, the flesh, the sinews, the synovial fluid,
dn16:6.23.5: neither charcoal was evident, nor was ash of the body left over.
dn16:6.23.6: Only two of those five-hundred pairs of clothes were not consumed, that on the inside and that on the outside.
dn16:6.23.7: When the Fortunate One’s body was burnt a shower of water appeared in the sky, and the Fortunate One’s funeral pyre was extinguished.
dn16:6.23.8: Also after water rose from a well, the Fortunate One’s funeral pyre was extinguished.
dn16:6.23.9: Also the Mallas from Kusinārā extinguished the Fortunate One’s funeral pyre with all types of fragrant water.
dn16:6.23.10: Then the Mallas of Kusinārā, * after making an enclosure of spears in the Council Hall, and surrounding the Fortunate One’s bodily relics with bows, honoured, respected, revered, and worshipped (it) with dance, song, music, garlands, and perfumes.
dn16:6.24.1: The Magadhan King Ajātasattu, the son of Lady Wisdom, heard:
dn16:6.24.2: “The Fortunate One, it seems, has attained Final Emancipation in Kusinārā.”
dn16:6.24.3: Then the Magadhan King Ajātasattu, the son of Lady Wisdom, sent a message to the Mallas of Kusinārā, (saying):
dn16:6.24.4: “The Fortunate One was a Noble, and I also am a Noble, I am worthy of a share of the Fortunate One’s bodily relics, I will make a Shrine and hold a festival for the bodily relics.”
dn16:6.24.5: Then the Licchavīs of Vesālī heard:
dn16:6.24.6: “The Fortunate One, it seems, has attained Final Emancipation in Kusinārā.”
dn16:6.24.7: Then the Licchavīs of Vesālī sent a message to the Mallas of Kusinārā, (saying):
dn16:6.24.8: “The Fortunate One was a Noble, and we also are Nobles, we are worthy of a share of the Fortunate One’s bodily relics, we will make a Shrine and hold a festival for the bodily relics.”
dn16:6.24.9: Then the Sakyas of Kapilavatthu heard:
dn16:6.24.10: “The Fortunate One, it seems, has attained Final Emancipation in Kusinārā.” Then the Sakyas of Kapilavatthu
dn16:6.24.11: sent a message to the Mallas of Kusinārā, (saying):
dn16:6.24.12: “The Fortunate One was our foremost relative, we are worthy of a share of the Fortunate One’s bodily relics, we will make a Shrine and hold a festival for the bodily relics.”
dn16:6.24.13: Then the Bulas of Allakappa heard:
dn16:6.24.14: “The Fortunate One, it seems, has attained Final Emancipation in Kusinārā.”
dn16:6.24.15: Then the Bulas of Allakappa sent a message to the Mallas of Kusinārā, (saying):
dn16:6.24.16: “The Fortunate One was a Noble, and we also are Nobles, we are worthy of a share of the Fortunate One’s bodily relics, we will make a Shrine and hold a festival for the bodily relics.”
dn16:6.24.17: Then the Koliyas of Rāmagāma heard:
dn16:6.24.18: “The Fortunate One, it seems, has attained Final Emancipation in Kusinārā.”
dn16:6.24.19: Then the Koliyas of Rāmagāma sent a message to the Mallas of Kusinārā, (saying):
dn16:6.24.20: “The Fortunate One was a Noble, and we also are Nobles, we are worthy of a share of the Fortunate One’s bodily relics, we will make a Shrine and hold a festival for the bodily relics.”
dn16:6.24.22: “The Fortunate One, it seems, has attained Final Emancipation in Kusinārā.”
dn16:6.24.23: Then the brahmin Veṭhadīpaka sent a message to the Mallas of Kusinārā, (saying):
dn16:6.24.24: “The Fortunate One was a Noble, and I am a brahmin, I am worthy of a share of the Fortunate One’s bodily relics, I will make a Shrine and hold a festival for the bodily relics.”
dn16:6.24.25: Then the Mallas of Pāvā heard:
dn16:6.24.26: “The Fortunate One, it seems, has attained Final Emancipation in Kusinārā.”
dn16:6.24.27: Then the Mallas of Pāvā sent a message to the Mallas of Kusinārā, (saying):
dn16:6.24.28: “The Fortunate One was a Noble, and we also are Nobles, we are worthy of a share of the Fortunate One’s bodily relics, we will make a Shrine and hold a festival for the bodily relics.”
dn16:6.25.1: After this was said, the Mallas of Kusinārā said this to their community and group:
dn16:6.25.2: “The Fortunate One has attained Final Emancipation in the area of our village, (but) we will not see a share of the Fortunate One’s bodily relics.”
dn16:6.25.3: After this was said, the brahmin Doṇa said this to their community and group:
dn16:6.25.4: “Listen, dear Sirs, to a sentence of mine:
dn16:6.25.5: Our Buddha was one who spoke about forbearance
dn16:6.25.6: * It is not good that there should be a battle
dn16:6.25.7: About sharing the relics of the Best Man.
dn16:6.25.8: * Let us united, in concord, dear Sirs,
dn16:6.25.9: With joyful minds, make eight shares (of the relics),
dn16:6.25.10: And set up Shrines in every direction
dn16:6.25.11: (So that) many people may gain faith in the Visionary One.”
dn16:6.25.12: * “Now, brahmin, you must divide the Fortunate One’s bodily relics in eight equal divisions.”
dn16:6.25.13: “Certainly, dear Sir,” said Doṇa the brahmin, after replying to that community and group, and dividing the Fortunate One’s bodily relics in eight equal divisions, he said this to that community and group:
dn16:6.25.14: “Please give me this urn, dear Sirs, and I also will make a Shrine and hold a festival for the urn.”
dn16:6.25.15: They gave the urn to Doṇa the brahmin.
dn16:6.26.1: Then the Moriyā of Pepper Wood heard:
dn16:6.26.2: “The Fortunate One, it seems, has attained Final Emancipation in Kusinārā.”
dn16:6.26.3: Then the Moriyā of Pepper Wood sent a message to the Mallas of Kusinārā, (saying):
dn16:6.26.4: “The Fortunate One was a Noble, and we also are Nobles, we are worthy of a share of the Fortunate One’s bodily relics, we will make a Shrine and hold a festival for the bodily relics.”
dn16:6.26.5: “There are no more portions of the Fortunate One’s relics,
dn16:6.26.6: (instead) take the ashes from the Fortunate One’s body.”
dn16:6.26.7: Therefore they took away the ashes.
dn16:6.27.1: Then the Magadhan King Ajātasattu, the son of Lady Wisdom, made a Shrine for the Fortunate One’s bodily relics at Rājagaha and held a festival.
dn16:6.27.2: The Licchavīs from Vesālī made a Shrine for the Fortunate One’s bodily relics at Vesālī and held a festival. The Sakyas from Kapilavatthu
dn16:6.27.3: made a Shrine for the Fortunate One’s bodily relics at Kapilavatthu and held a festival.
dn16:6.27.4: The Bulas of Allakappa made a Shrine for the Fortunate One’s bodily relics at Allakappa and held a festival. The Koliyas of Rāmagāma
dn16:6.27.5: made a Shrine for the Fortunate One’s bodily relics at Rāmagāma and held a festival.
dn16:6.27.6: The Veṭhadīpaka brahmin made a Shrine for the Fortunate One’s bodily relics at Veṭṭhadīpa and held a festival.
dn16:6.27.7: The Mallas of Pāvā made a Shrine for the Fortunate One’s bodily relics at Pāvā and held a festival.
dn16:6.27.8: The Mallas of Kusinārā made a Shrine for the Fortunate One’s bodily relics at Kusinārā and held a festival.
dn16:6.27.9: Doṇa the brahmin made a Shrine for the urn and held a festival.
dn16:6.27.10: The Moriyās of Pepper Wood made a Shrine for the ashes at Pepper Wood and held a festival.
dn16:6.27.11: Thus there were eight Shrines for the bodily relics, the Urn Shrine was the ninth, and the Ashes Shrine was the tenth,
dn16:6.27.12: and so it was in former times.
dn16:6.28.1: (There were) eight measures of the Visionary’s relics,
dn16:6.28.2: Seven measures are honoured in Jambudīpa,
dn16:6.28.3: One measure of the most Noble Man
dn16:6.28.4: The King of the Dragons honours in Rāmagāma.
dn16:6.28.5: One tooth is worshipped in the Heavens,
dn16:6.28.6: And one is honoured in the city of Gandhāra,
dn16:6.28.7: A further one in the realm of the Kaliṅga King,
dn16:6.28.8: And the King of the Dragons honours one more.
dn16:6.28.9: Through the power (of these relics) this Lovely Earth
dn16:6.28.10: Is decorated like a most excellent hall.
dn16:6.28.11: Thus this body of the Visionary One,
dn16:6.28.12: (Is) well esteemed by those who respect the respectable.
dn16:6.28.13: Honoured by Lords of Divinities, Lords of Dragons, and Kings,
dn16:6.28.14: (The relics are) honoured by true Lords of Men,
dn16:6.28.15: Worship those (relics) after holding up your hands,
dn16:6.28.16: A Buddha is rare even in a hundred aeons.
dn16:6.28.18: the hair, and body hair (relics) were
dn16:6.28.19: Carried off successively by the Divinities to the (various) Universes.
dn16:6.28.21: The Discourse about the Great Emancipation, The Third (in the Mahāvagga section of the Long Discourses) is Finished.
